IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r1.claim: The commentators take ذي ظفر as every bird with a claw and every livestock animal with a hoof; calling a hoof a nail is metaphorical.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r1.anchor: أي كل ذي مخلب من الطير، وكل ذي حافر من الدواب كذلك قال المفسرون

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r2.speaker: الشاعر الآخر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses حافر for a foot, supporting the metaphorical naming of a hoof as a nail.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r2.anchor: كما قال الآخر وذكر ضيفا طرقه :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r3.speaker: الشاعر الآخر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r3.claim: An unnamed poet calls feet أظلاف, although that word properly belongs to sheep and cattle hooves.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r3.anchor:
وقال آخر :
سأمنعها أو سوف أجعل أمرها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r4.claim: Arab idiom calls a man غليظ المشافر, meaning thick-lipped, although مشافر properly names camel lips.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r4.anchor: والعرب تقول للرجل: (هو غليظ المشافر) تريد الشفتين، والمشافر للإبل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r5.speaker: الحطيئة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r5.claim: Al-Hutayʾa’s use of مشافره for a man’s lips witnesses the camel-word’s metaphorical extension.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r5.anchor:
وقال الحطيئة :
قروا جارك العيمان لما جفوته

ITQAN:v2p566/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r16.claim: الحوايا is the plural of حاوية, or alternatively حاوياء.

STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r18.claim: Later passages reject arbitrary Makkan meat prohibitions and child sacrifice, replacing them with simpler revealed dietary rules and the commands and prohibitions in 6:151–153.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r18.anchor: several verses in the latter half of the sūrah address the arbitrary restrictions on the consumption of certain kinds of meat as observed by the Makkan idolaters—along with the pre-Islamic Makkan practice of “slaying their children”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.claim: Revelation identifies the specific forbidden animals in Abraham's religion; Jewish prohibitions match these except restrictions imposed on them for rebellion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.anchor: What was prohibited to the Jews was the same as prohibited in the religion of Abraham (sws) except the ones that were prohibited to them because of their rebelliousness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.claim: Israelites were additionally forbidden some wholesome foods as punishment for rebellion; these restrictions no longer apply in Islam, and Jews had been promised their removal through God's final messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.anchor: some pure and wholesome things too were forbidden to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.claim: The Torah passages describe a ban on animal fat; the Qur'anic exception covers fat inseparable from meat or attached to the back, intestines, or bone, while the Torah's absolute restriction appears to be a rabbinic addition.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.anchor: In my opinion, this harsh and strict view is actually of the rabbis and scholars of the Jews

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p141.claim: Since some blood remains attached to meat, the phrase “blood poured forth” limits the restriction to natural bounds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.claim: God promised in Sūrah al-Māʾidah that accepting the final messenger would lift Israelite burdens because he would restore Abraham's natural religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.anchor: if they profess faith in the last messenger, these burdens would be lifted from them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.claim: Idolaters invent prohibitions without evidence, while Jewish prohibitions punished rebellion; Islam lifts both extremes and allows what is pure according to nature and reason.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p143.anchor: This religion is devoid of the innovations of the Idolaters and the extremities of the Jews

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.claim: He notes that the nails of animals that do not hunt have a term in contrast with the claws of those that do.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.anchor: that do not hunt are called

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.claim: Jewish law allowed quadrupeds only if they had split hooves and chewed cud; the term for animals with nails refers to intact hooves, so camels and rabbits were forbidden to Jews despite being lawful in Abraham's religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.anchor: among the Jews, only those quadruped animals were lawful which had split hooves and which chewed the cud

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.claim: These food restrictions punished Israelite rebellion rather than reflecting inherent impurity; repeated questioning and evasions made their law burdensome, described as “burdens and shackles” at 7:157.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.anchor: animals with nails and the fat were not unlawful to the Jews because they had some intrinsic reason for prohibition

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.claim: The Israelites also had stricter restrictions on sea animals, allowing only fish with fins and scales, and prohibited waterfowl and other birds beyond hunting birds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p142.anchor: sea animals having fins and scales were lawful and all the rest were forbidden

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r13.claim: Ẓufr has several vowelings and forms, including ẓufūr, plural aẓfār and aẓāfīr, and describes a long-nailed man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r13.anchor: الظفر: معروف وهو بضم الظاء والفاء وبسكون الفاء وبكسرهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r14.claim: The morphology of ḥawāyā admits several analyses as plurals of ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiyya; it denotes coils in sheep bellies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p664/r14.anchor: الحوايا: إن قدر وزنها فواعل فجمع حاوية كراوية وروايا أو جمع حاوياء

SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.claim: The excepted noun takes accusative because it is removed from the preceding set, is not an adjective, and is governed by the prior clause, like درهما after twenty.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.anchor: وانتصب الأب إذ لم يكن داخلا فيما دخل فيه

SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.claim: In an affirmative sentence إلا أبوك cannot be an appositional replacement; after negation, ما أتاني القوم إلا أبوك is valid as though the exception alone were stated.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهمخرجمماأدخلتفيهغيرهفعملفيهم.anchor: وإنما جاز ما أتاني القوم إلا أبوك

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r1.claim: Fronting على الذين هادوا before حرمنا marks restriction for some grammarians, including al-Zamakhshari and al-Razi; al-Razi explicitly notes the governed phrase precedes its verb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r1.anchor: متعلق بحرمنا، وهو يفيد الاختصاص عند بعضهم كالزمخشري والرازي

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r2.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r2.claim: The common recitation uses ظفر, which the author calls the highest of five Arabic forms for the word.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r2.anchor: وفي " الظفر " لغات خمس، أعلاها: ظفر وهي قراءة العامة

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r3.speaker: الحسن، أُبَيّ بن كعب، الأعرج
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r3.claim: A form with sukūn on the middle radical, easing the form with ḍamma, is read by al-Hasan in one report, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and al-Aʿraj.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r3.anchor: وظفر بسكون العين وهي تخفيف المضمومها، وبها قرأ الحسن في رواية وأبي بن كعب والأعرج

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r4.speaker: أبو السمال
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r4.claim: A form with kasra on both ظاء and فاء is attributed by al-Wahidi to Abu al-Sammal.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r4.anchor: وظفر بكسر الظاء والفاء، ونسبها الواحدي لأبي السمال قراءة

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r5.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r5.claim: Another form has kasra on ظاء and sukūn on فاء, easing the kasra; readers also attribute this recitation to al-Hasan.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r5.anchor: وظفر بكسر الظاء وسكون الفاء وهي تخفيف المكسورها

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r6.claim: أظفور is a fifth lexical form, though the author knows of no recitation using it; a poetic line attests the word.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r6.anchor: واللغة الخامسة أظفور ولم يقرأ بها فيما علمت، وأنشدوا على ذلك قول الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r7.claim: The triliteral plural is أظفار; أظافير is the regular plural of أظفور, while أظافر without long ا is irregular.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r7.anchor: وجمع الثلاثي أظفار، وجمع أظفور أظافير وهو القياس، وأظافر من غير مد

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r8.claim: A poetic fragment, العينين والعواور, is cited as a parallel for the non-analogical plural pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r8.anchor: وأظافر من غير مد وليس بقياس، وهذا كقوله

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r9.claim: من البقر may coordinate with كل ذي and attach to the first حرمنا, with the second clause explaining the partitive phrase; or it may attach to the later حرمنا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r9.anchor: فيه وجهان أحدهما: أنه معطوف على

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r10.claim: Abu al-Baqa forbids attaching من البقر to the second verb; the Shaykh rejects that restriction, distinguishing its position after the verb from an alleged required position after the object and allowing either order.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وكأنه توهم أن عود الضمير

SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r11.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r11.claim: The Shaykh supports the order with examples ضرب غلام المرأة أبوها and غلام المرأة ضرب أبوها: a prepositional phrase and object can exchange order without violating grammatical rank.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146/r11.anchor: فليس بممنوع بل يجوز ذلك كما جاز: " ضرب غلام المرأة أبوها "

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r1.claim: The poetic construction supports obligatory fronting of the adverb so a subject-attached pronoun can refer to the noun governed by that adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r1.anchor: فقدم الظرف وجوبا لعود الضمير الذي اتصل بالفاعل على المجرور بالظرف

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r2.claim: The possessive dual in their fats adds emphasis to restriction and connection; the simpler wording would already identify the fats as those of cattle and sheep.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r2.anchor: تفيد الدلالة على تأكيد التخصيص والربط، إذ لو أتى في الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r3.claim: ما is a relative pronoun in the accusative as a connected exception from the fats: fat carried on the backs was not forbidden.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r3.anchor: موصولة في محل نصب على الاستثناء المتصل من الشحوم

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r4.claim: A proposed parsing makes the relative clause an adjective of an omitted noun, but the author objects that the Shaykh elsewhere says ما is not described by an adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r4.anchor: وفيه نظر، لأنه هو قد نص على أنه لا يوصف

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, an omitted noun is understood as fat; من الشحم is a semantic rather than formal adjective, since explicit wording would be circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r5.anchor: وهذا الجار هو وصف معنوي لا صناعي فإنه لو أظهر

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r6.claim: The dual may treat cattle and sheep collectively as two referents, as in the phrase your two hearts, without regard to their members.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r6.anchor: بالنسبة إلى ضمير البقر والغنم من غير نظر إلى جمعيتهما في المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, ظُهُور is plural because cattle and sheep are plural in sense, like the heads of two rams; on this analysis a dual is impossible.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#2/r7.anchor: لأن المضاف إليه جمع في المعنى، فهو مثل " قطعت رؤوس الكبشين " فالتثنية

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r1.claim: The apparent parsing, attributed to al-Kisāʾī, puts الحوايا in the nominative coordinated with ظهورهما: what the entrails carry is also exempt.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r1.anchor: وهو قول الكسائي أنها في موضع رفع عطفا على

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r2.speaker: جماعة قليلة
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r2.claim: A minority parses الحوايا in the accusative, coordinated with شحومهما, making the entrails and what is mixed with bone prohibited rather than excepted.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r2.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب جماعة قليلة، وتكون " أو " فيه كالتي في قوله

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r3.claim: On the accusative coordination, أو conveys that each item is independently forbidden, as in 76:24; using واو might imply that only their combination is prohibited.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: حرمت عليهم الثروب وأحل لهم ما حملت الظهور

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī compares أو in the accusative analysis to the permissive command to sit with al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " أو بمنزلتها في قولهم:

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r5.claim: Grammarians take أو in that example as permission to sit with both or either; if الحوايا coordinates with شحومهما, the better reading is that أو specifies the categories forbidden.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وقال النحويون " أو " في هذا المثال للإباحة

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains the rhetoric: لا تطع زيدا وعمرا may forbid only their joint obedience, whereas أو means each person is independently not to be obeyed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r6.anchor: لأنك إذا قلت: " لا تطع زيدا وعمرا " فجائز أن تكون نهيتني

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ had already said أو here means واو, to detail their different doctrines or the different locations of the fats, as in 2:135.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#3/r7.anchor: فقد سبقه إلى ذلك أبو البقاء فإنه قال: و " أو " هنا بمعنى الواو

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r1.speaker: مكي وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r1.claim: A third parsing puts الحوايا in the accusative coordinated with the excepted ما; Makkī transmits it and Abū al-Baqāʾ begins with it before giving another view.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r1.anchor: نقله مكي، وأبو البقاء بدأ به ثم قال

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects coordinating الحوايا with the prohibited fats, saying neither wording nor meaning supports that analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ردا على هذا القول أعني كون الحوايا نسقا على شحومهما

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows an elided مضاف, understanding the phrase as the fats of the entrails, like asking the town for its people in 12:82.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r3.anchor: ونقل الواحدي عن الفراء أنه قال: " يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بتقدير حذف المضاف

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r4.claim: In Abū ʿUbayd’s poetic analogy, الضوع coordinates with النئيم rather than البوم, like الحوايا with ما; the author says this entails a strained coordination with the exception.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r4.anchor: وحكى ابن الأنباري عن أبي عبيد أنه قال: قلت للفراء: هو بمنزلة قول الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r5.claim: Lexicographers identify الحوايا as animal bowels or dung, all that gathers and coils in the belly, or the round coil in a sheep’s belly.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r5.anchor: وأما ما يتعلق بمدلولها فقيل: هي المباعر، وقيل: المصارين والأمعاء

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r6.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r6.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī gives حوية and حاوية as singulars of الحوايا, without mentioning حاوياء.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: هي الحوية والحاوية ولم يذكر الحاوياء

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r7.speaker: ابن السكيت
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt lists حاوية, حوية, and حاوياء as possible singulars of حوايا.

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r8.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r8.claim: Al-Fārisī allows حوايا to be the plural of each of the three proposed singular forms.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r8.anchor: وقد جوز الفارسي أن يكون جمعا لكل واحد من الثلاثة

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r9.claim: Some speakers also derive حوايا from حوية by analogy with the saddle pad placed on a camel’s back; the line by Jarīr is introduced as evidence for حاوياء.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#4/r9.anchor: ومنهم من يقول حوية وحوايا مثل الحوية التي توضع على ظهر البعير

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r1.claim: Jarīr’s line uses حاوياء as a singular behind حوايا; Abū Bakr Ibn al-Anbārī recites a second line containing حاويائه.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r1.anchor: تضغو الخنانيص والغول التي أكلت في حاوياء

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r2.claim: The line recited by Abū Bakr Ibn al-Anbārī attests the form حاويائه.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r2.anchor: كأن نقيق الحب في حاويائه فحيح الأفاعي

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r3.claim: If the singular is حاوية or حاوياء, حوايا has pattern فواعل from حواوي, with hamza substitution and subsequent vowel changes.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r3.anchor: فإن كان مفردها حاوية فوزنها فواعل كضاربة وضوارب

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r4.claim: If the singular is حوية, حوايا has pattern فعائل from حوائي; hamza and weak-final changes yield the same surface form by a different derivation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r4.anchor: وإن قلنا إن مفردها حوية فوزنها فعائل كطرائف

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r5.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ coordinates this phrase with the excepted ما and identifies it as the tail fat; another sense is fat in the flank, eye, ear, or limbs.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#5/r5.anchor: ورأى الفراء فيه أنه منصوب نسقا على " ما " المستثناة

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r1.speaker: الحوفي ومكي وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r1.claim: One parsing supplies an omitted subject: the matter is that. The author understands Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s unspecified nominative analysis this way because the alternative is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r1.anchor: الأمر ذلك، قاله الحوفي ومكي وأبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r2.claim: Another parsing makes ذلك the subject and the following clause its predicate, with an omitted object resuming it; the author calls this weak.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r2.anchor: العائد محذوف، أي: ذلك جزيناهموه، قاله أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes ذلك as an accusative cognate object meaning that punishment.

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r4.speaker: ابن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r4.claim: Ibn Mālik objects that a demonstrative pointing to a verbal noun should be followed by that noun, as in ضربت ذلك الضرب.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r4.anchor: نقله ابن مالك وهو أن المصدر إذا أشير إليه وجب أن يتبع

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r5.speaker: ابن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r5.claim: Ibn Mālik rejects the defense of al-Mutanabbī’s هذي برزت as a demonstrative for a source, since the source noun does not follow it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r5.anchor: هذي برزت فهجت رسيسا ثم انصرفت وما شفيت نسيسا

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r6.claim: The author rejects Ibn Mālik’s rule, citing a poet’s ذاك as a demonstrative for the source of خال without a following source noun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r6.anchor: إلا أن رد ابن مالك ليس بصحيح لورود اسم الإشارة مشارا به إلى المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء ومكي
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī also parse ذلك as an accusative governed by جزيناهم, without saying whether it is a second object or cognate object.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#6/r7.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء ومكي: إنه في موضع نصب بجزيناهم، ولم يبينا

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r1.claim: The omitted complement may mean that God is truthful in completing their requital in the afterlife, alluding to the Jews’ false claim of following Israel’s prohibitions.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r1.anchor: أي: لصادقون في إتمام جزائهم في الآخرة إذ هو تعريض بكذبهم

SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r2.claim: Alternatively, God is truthful in informing about them, or no complement is supplied because truthfulness is intrinsic to God.
SAMIN-DURR:6:146#7/r2.anchor: في إخبارنا عنهم ذلك، ولا يقدر له معمول

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r1.claim: The animals meant by every clawed creature are camels and ostriches, since ostriches have claws like camels.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r1.anchor: ئعنى به الإبل والنعام، لأن النعام ذوات ظفر كالإبل

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r2.claim: One reported view forbids the caul fats and allows the other fats carried on the backs.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r2.anchor: فقال بعض الناس:. حرمت عليهم الثروب، وأحل لهم ما سواها مما

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r3.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the entrails; the singular is given as ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiyya.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r3.anchor: وهي المباعر واحدها حاوية وحاوياء وحوية

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r4.claim: Fat mixed with bone includes tail fat; this is the more common of the two opinions.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r4.anchor: نحو شحم الإلية. وهذا أكثر القولين

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r5.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r5.claim: Another group construes the categories after the caul prohibition as including back-carried fat, entrail fat, or fat mixed with bone, and explicitly says what the backs carry is not forbidden.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r5.anchor: وقال قوم حرمت عليهم الثروب. وأحل لهم ما حملت الظهور وصارت الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r6.claim: Here aw marks permissive alternatives: each named person or category can independently be avoided or selected; it need not mean that all are treated only as a joint set.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r6.anchor: دخلت على طريق الإباحة، كما قال جل وعز

ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r7.claim: The disjunctive wording is more emphatic than wa: in a prohibition, aw can mean none of the listed parties should be obeyed, while in an instruction to associate, any or all listed people are suitable.
ZAJJAJ:v2p301/r7.anchor: فليس المعنى أني آمرك بمجالسة واحد منهم، ولكن معنى

ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n137/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n137/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n137/r1.claim: Razi reads the construction as making this dietary prohibition specific to Jews and excluding believers of later times.
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n137/r1.anchor: The construction of the above sentence makes it clear that this prohibition was imposed specifically on the Jews, to the exclusion of believers of later times (Razi).

ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n138/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n138/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n138/r1.claim: Asad compares the restriction with Leviticus 7:23, which forbids all fat from ox, sheep, or goat.
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n138/r1.anchor: Cf. Leviticus vii, 23 (where, however, "all manner" of fat of ox, sheep or goat is declared forbidden).

ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n139/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n139/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:146#n139/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to 3:93 for a related discussion.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p517/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p517/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p517/r1.claim: A clipped preceding discussion says the nose is restrained by shackles, or cautiously suggests the restraint concerns a proud, upturned nose being brought down; its context is missing from this excerpt.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p517/r1.anchor: الأنف فيه إلى قيدِ بالأغلال. أو لعل وجه الاحتراز فيه أنه الشامخ الأنف المنكس رأسه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r1.claim: Al-anʿām refers to cattle, sheep, goats, and camels; bahīma is broader, covering living creatures without reason, with livestock as one subset.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r1.anchor: الأنعام هي البقر والغنم والمعز والإبل (ثمانية أزواج) . البهيمة من ذوات الأرواح، ما لا عقل له

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r2.speaker: قسم من أهل اللغة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r2.claim: Some linguists use bahīmat al-anʿām for animals analogous to livestock, including gazelles and wild cattle, and other edible ruminants without fangs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1040/r2.anchor: قسم من أهل اللغة قالوا هي ما ماثل الأنعام وأدخلوا بها الظباء وبقر الوحش

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the animals with an un-split hoof or claw as camels and ostriches; their feet have a single claw, and the ban also covers ducks and similar birds whose toes are not split.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كل ذي ظفر ﴾ قال الإبل والنعام ظفر يد البعير ورجله والنعام أيضا كذلك قال وحرم عليهم من الطير البط

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أو الحوايا ﴾ قال هو البقر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r2.claim: After explaining that prohibitions rest on divine revelation, the passage says God also imposed dietary prohibitions on earlier communities, as on this community in the preceding verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r2.anchor: مناسبة هذه لما قبلها أنه لما بين أن التحريم إنما يستند للوحي الإلهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r3.claim: The wording حرمنا refutes the Jews' claim that God prohibited nothing for them and that they only adopted what Israel had forbidden himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r3.anchor: إن الله لم يحرم علينا شيئا وإنما حرمنا على أنفسنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وقتادة والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r4.claim: They identify the category as cloven-hoofed animals such as camels and ostriches, and animals without split toes such as ducks and geese; al-Zajjāj chose this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وقتادة والسدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the phrase to camels, a restriction Abū Ḥayyān calls weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هي الإبل خاصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies only ostriches and wild asses; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this as too narrow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي النعامة وحمار الوحش وهو ضعيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r7.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī includes birds of prey with talons, hoofed beasts, and fanged predators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كل ذي مخلب من الطير وذي حافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r8.speaker: القتبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r8.claim: Al-Qutaybī takes ظفر as a metaphorical name for a hoof, covering every hoofed animal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r8.anchor: وقال القتبي: الظفر هنا بمنزلة الحافر يدخل فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r9.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r9.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes non-hunting animals as ذي ظفر and hunting animals as ذي مخلب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r9.anchor: وقال ثعلب: كل ما لا يصيد فهو ذو ظفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r10.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r10.claim: Al-Naqqāsh objects that Thaʿlab's distinction is inconsistent because a lion has claws.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r10.anchor: قال النقاش: هذا غير مطرد لأن الأسد ذو ظفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines the category as any animal or bird with a digit; because some such animals were lawful before, injustice brought a general prohibition on them for the Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ما له أصبع من دابة أو طائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r12.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects hoof as the meaning because cattle and sheep have hooves yet the verse permits them; he instead means predatory claws and talons, a Jewish-specific ban, and rejects solitary reports banning them for Muslims as contrary to the Qur'an, supporting Mālik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: حمل الظفر على الحافر ضعيف لأن الحافر لا يكاد يسمى ظفرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r13.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Rāzī's assumptions about the term's restriction, the claimed exclusivity to Jews, and the claim that the hadith conflicts with the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r13.anchor: لا نسلم تخصيص ذي الظفر بما قاله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r14.claim: Whichever animal category the earlier interpreters assign to ذي ظفر, they take its meat, fat, and all of it to be forbidden to the Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r14.anchor: وكل من فسر الظفر بما فسره من ذوي الأقوال السابقة بذاهب إلى تحريم لحم ما فسره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r15.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r15.claim: Some commentators posit an omitted object: the ban is on prey caught by an untrained clawed hunter, not on the clawed animal itself; Abū Ḥayyān calls this contrary to the apparent wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r15.anchor: وذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن ذلك على حذف مضاف وليس المحرم ذا الظفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r16.speaker: أبي الحسن والأعرج والحسن وأبو السمال قعنب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r16.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj, as well as al-Ḥasan and Abū al-Sammāl Quʿnub, read ظفر with a still fāʾ; al-Ḥasan also has the reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p676/r16.anchor: وقرأ أبي الحسن والأعرج ظفر بسكون الفاء والحسن أيضا وأبو السمال قعنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r1.claim: من can modify the later حرمنا although it precedes that verb; the construction is like أخذت من زيد ماله, while placing it after the verb would sound unusual.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r1.anchor: ويتعلق من بحرمنا المتأخرة ولا يجب تقدمها على العامل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r2.claim: An alternative coordinates ومن البقر والغنم with كل ذي ظفر, attaching من to the first حرمنا and making the second clause explain which parts were prohibited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ومن البقر والغنم معطوفا على كل ذي ظفر فيتعلق من بحرمنا الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects attachment of من to the second verb and parses the phrase as coordinated with كل ذي ظفر, with the second clause specifying the prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: لا يجوز أن يكون من البقر متعلقا بحرمنا الثانية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān answers that a prepositional phrase and an object are both complements, so either may precede the other; an attached pronoun can require the order.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r4.anchor: لكن عن ماذا أما عن الفعل فمسلم وأما عن المفعول فغير مسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r5.claim: The poetic example وقد ركدت وسط السماء نجومها shows an adverb fronted before the subject because that subject contains a pronoun referring back to the adverb's noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r5.anchor: وقد ركدت وسط السماء نجومها فقدم الظرف وجوبا لعود الضمير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r6.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r6.claim: Mālik prohibits eating fat from animals slaughtered by Jews; another report from him gives mere dislike.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r6.anchor: فعن مالك منع أكل الشحم من ذبائحهم وروي عنه الكراهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r7.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r7.claim: Some allow the fat from Jewish slaughter, even fat they themselves regard as forbidden if a Muslim ordered the slaughter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r7.anchor: وأباح ذلك بعض الناس من ذبائحهم ومن ذبحهم ما هو عليهم حرام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r8.speaker: ابن حبيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r8.claim: Ibn Ḥabīb says a ban known from scripture also bars the fat from their slaughter, but a ban known only from their statements does not bar it for Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r8.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب: ما كان معلوما تحريمه عليهم من كتابنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r9.claim: The apparent implication of 5:5 is that fat from their slaughter is not lawful because fat is not included in the People of the Book's food; reading their food as slaughter alone is far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p677/r9.anchor: فظاهر قوله: وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r1.claim: The exception means the fat carried on the backs of cattle and sheep is permitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r1.anchor: إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أي إلا الشحم الذي حملته ظهورهما البقر والغنم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies it as fat attached to the back and to the side inside the belly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو مما علق بالظهر من الشحم وبالجنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r3.claim: Another view identifies it as the fatty strips carried on the back, which were not forbidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r3.anchor: وقيل: سمين الظهر وهي الشرائح التي على الظهر من الشحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r4.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r4.claim: Al-Suddī and Abū Ṣāliḥ identify the exempt back fat as tails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r4.anchor: وقال السدي وأبو صالح: الإليات مما حملت ظهورهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r5.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says أو الحوايا is coordinated with ظهورهما, meaning fat carried by the entrails; Abū Ḥayyān calls this the apparent parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r5.anchor: هو معطوف على ظهورهما قاله الكسائي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r6.claim: These authorities identify الحوايا as the animal's innards or bowels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن جبير والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد: هي المباعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā defines الحوايا as everything contained in the belly that gathers and forms a curve.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى: هو كل ما تحويه البطن فاجتمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd also identifies الحوايا as بنات اللبن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد أيضا: هي بنات اللبن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r9.claim: Another explanation takes الحوايا as intestines and bowels bearing fat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r9.anchor: وقيل: الأمعاء والمصارين التي عليها الشحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r10.claim: The phrase is coordinated with ما حملت ظهورهما; Abū Ḥayyān takes the three exceptions as exclusions from the prohibited fats and thus lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r10.anchor: هو معطوف على ما حملت ظهورهما بعظم هو شحم الإلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r11.speaker: السدي وابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r11.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Jurayj identify the fat mixed with bone as tail fat lying on the coccyx.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r11.anchor: هو شحم الإلية لأنه على العصعص قاله السدي وابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj also identifies it as side fat, or fat on the limbs, sides, head, eyes, and ears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r12.anchor: أو شحم الجنب أو كل شحم في القوائم والجنب والرأس والعينين والأذنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r13.claim: Another view identifies the phrase as marrow in the bone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r13.anchor: أو مخ العظم والظاهر أن هذه الثلاثة مستثناة من الشحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān's apparent reading treats the back, entrails, and bone-mixed fat as three exceptions from the ban and therefore lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r14.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الثلاثة مستثناة من الشحم فهي حلال لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r15.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r15.claim: An alternative coordinates الحوايا and bone-mixed fat with شحومهما, making them prohibited and leaving only back fat as the exception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r15.anchor: وقيل: أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم معطوف على قوله شحومهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī compares أو to its use in ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا and جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r16.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وأو بمنزلتها في قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r17.speaker: النحويون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r17.claim: Grammarians call أو permissive in the sitting example, allowing both or either; if these phrases coordinate with the prohibited fats, Abū Ḥayyān prefers treating أو as specifying the prohibited categories.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r17.anchor: وقال النحويون: أو في هذا المثال للإباحة فيجوز له أن يجالسهما معا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r18.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports a view coordinating الحوايا with the fats and thus prohibiting it, but says neither wording nor meaning supports that view; Abū Ḥayyān notes he gives no explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p678/r18.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وقال بعض الناس أو الحوايا معطوف على الشحوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says ذلك is nominative; al-Ḥawfī allows an implied مبتدأ, or an accusative direct object of جزيناهم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ذلك في موضع رفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses ذلك as accusative governed by جزيناهم but does not specify its syntactic role; the reported subject reading جزيناهموه is weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: ذلك في موضع نصب ب جزيناهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases ذلك as that punishment, namely the prohibition of good things, which makes the demonstrative a cognate-like object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ذلك الجزاء جزيناهم وهو تحريم الطيبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r4.claim: Given Ibn Mālik's rule that a demonstrative cannot stand alone for a verbal noun without a following noun, the cognate-object analysis of ذلك is invalid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r4.anchor: وزعم ابن مالك أن اسم الإشارة لا ينتصب مشارا به إلى المصدر إلا وأتبع بالمصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān explains البغي here as oppression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r5.anchor: والبغي هنا الظلم. وقال الحسن: الكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī specifies their oppression as killing prophets without right, taking usury, and consuming people's wealth unlawfully; he links this to 4:160 and treats the prohibition as punishment for sins and defiance toward prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: هو قتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وأخذهم الربا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r8.speaker: القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that a prohibition cannot punish a prior crime, since imposing duties exposes people to reward and is therefore benevolent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r8.anchor: قال القاضي: نفس التحريم لا يكون عقوبة على جرم صدر منهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān replies that withholding benefit can be imposed either to expose someone to reward or because of an earlier offense; both explanations are plausible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r9.anchor: والجواب: أن المنع من الانتفاع يمكن لمن يرى استحقاق الثواب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r10.claim: The statement affirms that God truly reported what He prohibited for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r10.anchor: وإنا لصادقون في الإخبار عما حرمنا عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the statement insinuates that the Jews lie when they claim God prohibited nothing and that they merely followed Israel's self-imposed ban; it refutes them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: إخبار يتضمن التعريض بكذبهم في قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r12.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r12.claim: Al-Tabrīzī takes the statement as truthfulness in completing their promised afterlife punishment; the dietary restriction is an advance punishment in this world, followed by a great punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r12.anchor: وقال التبريزي: وإنا لصادقون في إتمام جزائهم في الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God does not break threats to sinners any more than promises to the obedient, and fulfilled the threat by punishing their rebellion; Abū Ḥayyān labels this Muʿtazilite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p679/r13.anchor: وقال الزمخشري وإنا لصادقون فيما أوعدنا به العصاة لا نخلفه كما لا نخلف ما وعدناه أهل الطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r1.claim: The prohibition is addressed specifically to the Jews, not to other peoples before or after them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r1.anchor: أي اليهود خاصة لا على من عداهم من الأولين والآخرين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جرير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r2.claim: They explain an animal with an undivided hoof or claw, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r2.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وابن جرير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the referent to camels.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r3.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أنه الأبل فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r4.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī includes all predators, dogs, cats, and animals that hunt with their claws.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r4.anchor: الجبائي : يدخل فيه كل السباع والكلاب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r5.speaker: القتبي والبلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r5.claim: Al-Qutaybī and al-Balkhī mean clawed birds and hoofed beasts, using ‘nail’ figuratively for hoof; the Imam considers this unlikely.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r5.anchor: القتبي والبلخي أنه ذو المخلب من الطير وذو الحافر من الدواب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r6.claim: The generalization of the ban may itself be the punishment for wrongdoing, since some of these things were already prohibited.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r6.anchor: المسبب عن الظلم هو تعميم التحريم لأن البعض كان حراما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r7.claim: He also allows reading the phrase as every clawed animal that was lawful, on the stated contextual indication.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r7.anchor: يراد كل ذي ظفر حلال بقرينة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r8.claim: The statement confirms the earlier restriction of forbidden foods and refutes the Jews’ claim that the restrictions had applied since Noah and Abraham.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r8.anchor: تحقيق لما سلف من حصر المحرمات فيما فصل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r9.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r9.claim: Some scholars take the verse as completing the preceding argument: animal restrictions and rules about bahīra and sāʾiba were imposed on Jews specifically as punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r9.anchor: المحققين : إن ذلك تتميم لما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r10.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r10.claim: Al-Hasan reads ẓufur with ẓāʾ kasra and fāʾ sukūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r10.anchor: الحسن ( ظفر ) بكسر الظاء وسكون الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r11.speaker: أبو السماك
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r11.claim: Abū al-Sammāk reads both consonants with kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r11.anchor: أبو السماك بكسرهما وقريء كما قال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r12.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r12.claim: Another reading, cited by Abū al-Baqāʾ, has ẓāʾ ḍamma and fāʾ sukūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r12.anchor: قال أبو البقاء ظفر بضم الظاء وسكون الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r13.claim: The prohibited fats do not include meat; they are thin fat on intestines and rumen and kidney fat, though a broader sense is also reported.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r13.anchor: لا لحومهما فانها باقية على الحل والمراد بالشحوم ما يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r14.claim: ‘Of cattle and sheep’ attaches to the following ‘We prohibited’; naming the fats again adds connection and emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r14.anchor: ( من البقر ) متعلق بحرمنا بعده وكان يكفي حينئذ أن يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r15.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r15.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also permits attaching ‘of cattle’ to ‘every clawed animal,’ meaning some cattle, with the prohibition clause explaining what is forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47/r15.anchor: أبو البقاء وظاهر صنيعه اختياره مع أنه خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r1.claim: The exception concerns fat attached to the animals’ backs; grammarians differ whether it is connected or disconnected from ‘fats.’
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r1.anchor: ما علق بظهورهما والاستثناء منقطع أو متصل من الشحوم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa treats the exception as disconnected: someone swearing not to eat fat breaks the oath only by eating abdominal fat.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r2.anchor: عنه لو حلف لا يأكل شحما سحنث بشحم البطن فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r3.speaker: صاحباه
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa’s companions say eating back fat also breaks that oath because it is fat and melts in fire, supporting a connected exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r3.anchor: صاحباه فقالا يحنث بشحم الظهر أيضا لأنه شحم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r4.claim: The Imam favors disconnection: back fat is meat in reality, cooked and eaten as meat, and its seller is a butcher; this outweighs the usual presumption for a connected exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r4.anchor: وللامام رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه لحم حقيقة لأنه ينشأ من الدم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r5.claim: One explanation identifies al-ḥawāyā as the entrails or places where feces collect.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما أو المرابض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd explains al-ḥawāyā as the udder or places where milk gathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r6.anchor: كما روي عن ابن زيد أو المصارين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r7.speaker: غير واحد من أهل اللغة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r7.claim: Several lexicographers identify al-ḥawāyā as the intestines and bowels.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r7.anchor: المصارين والأمعاء كما قال غير واحد من أهل اللغة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r8.claim: For a connected exception, proponents supply ‘fats of the entrails’ or explain the word as the fat wrapped around them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r8.anchor: للقائل بالاتصال أن يقول العطف على تقدير مضاف أي شحوم الحوايا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r9.claim: Other grammarians allow coordinating al-ḥawāyā with either ‘their backs’ or ‘their fats.’
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r9.anchor: وجوز غير واحد أن يكون العطف على ( ظهورهما ) وأن يكون على ( شحومهما )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r10.speaker: بعض السلف
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r10.claim: Some early authorities take what is attached to bone as tail fat adjoining the coccyx; another explanation is marrow, though it is not ordinarily called fat.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r10.anchor: بعض السلف وهو يعطف قوله تعالى : ( أو ما أختلط بعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r11.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is variously analyzed as plural of ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiyya, each with a described pattern and sound changes.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r11.anchor: جمع حاوية كزاوية وزوايا ووزنه فواعل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r12.speaker: الفارسي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r12.claim: Al-Fārisī allows the plural to derive from any of the three proposed singulars, each attested; ‘or’ may also mean ‘and.’
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r12.anchor: الفارسي أن يكون جمعا لكل واحد من هذه الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r13.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r13.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ compares the conjunction to its use in ‘Be Jews or Christians,’ for distinguishing alternatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r13.anchor: أبو البقاء لتفصيل مذاهبهم نظيرها في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r14.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r14.claim: Al-Zajjāj says that when ‘or’ coordinates with fats, it expresses permissive choice, as in ‘do not obey a sinner or unbeliever.’
ALUSI-FULL:v8p47#2/r14.anchor: الزجاج : هي فيما إذا كان العطف على الشحوم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that ‘or’ makes each object independently unworthy of obedience: the phrasing prohibits obeying any one or all of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r1.anchor: كلهم أهل أن لايطاع فلا تطع واحدا منهم ولا تطع الجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r2.speaker: العلامة الثاني
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r2.claim: The Second Allāma reads ‘or’ like ‘sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn’: all listed items are equally within the ruling, rather than a choice to consume some.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r2.anchor: اختاره العلامة الثاني وقال الوجه أن يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r3.claim: Al-Ṭībī says attaching the three items to ‘fats’ puts all under prohibition except what was excepted; attaching them to the exception leaves only fats prohibited.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r3.anchor: وذكر الطيبي في حاصل كلام بعض المحققين في أو هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r4.claim: The claim that the latter construction permits eating two of the three is rejected: jurists and legal theorists recognize prohibited or permissible choices among alternatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r4.anchor: هذه الدعوى من العجب فان الحرام المخير

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r5.claim: ‘That’ may refer to requital, making it an accusative cognate object, or to prohibition, making it a second object of ‘requited’; the verb takes either a prepositional or direct object.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r6.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r6.claim: Ibn Mālik denies a demonstrative can refer to a verbal noun and be accusative without a following verbal noun; Abū Ḥayyān and al-Jalabī reject the restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r6.anchor: ابن مالك أن اسم الاشارة لا ينتصب مشارا به إلى المصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r7.speaker: أبو حيان والجلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and al-Jalabī confirm a demonstrative may point to a verbal noun without a following verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r7.anchor: أبو حيان والجلبي وصححا ورود اسم الاشارة مشارا به إلى المصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r8.claim: Other parses make ‘that’ the predicate of an omitted subject or a subject whose predicate omits its object pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r8.anchor: كون ذلك خبر مبتدأ مقدر أي الأمر ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r9.claim: Their wrongdoing includes killing prophets unjustly, taking usury despite its prohibition, and consuming people’s property wrongfully; each sin brought a further food prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r9.anchor: بسبب ظلمهم وهو قتلهم الانبياء بغير حق وأكلهم الربا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r10.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r10.claim: Another account says Israelite rulers barred the poor from birds and fats, so God prohibited those foods to them; withholding benefit may also serve a purpose or reflect earlier wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p48/r10.anchor: نقل علي بن إبراهيم في تفسيره أن ملوك بني اسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r1.claim: God is truthful in all reports, including the prohibition and its cause; some limit the reference to promise and threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r1.anchor: في جميع أخبارنا التي من جملتها الأخبار بالتحريم وبالبغي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r2.claim: The Imam uses the verse to support Mālik and many early authorities: only the four foods in the preceding verse are generally forbidden, and ‘claw’ means talon rather than hoof.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r2.anchor: وقوى الامام بهذه الآية ما ذهب اليه الامام مالك وكثير من السلف

ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r3.claim: He rejects ‘hoof’ because a hoof is hardly called a nail, and that reading would imply forbidding all hoofed animals despite the verse allowing cattle and sheep.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r4.claim: He argues that the restriction applies only to Jews: the construction conveys exclusivity, and otherwise singling them out is pointless; this would leave predators and clawed birds lawful for Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r4.anchor: والآية تفيد تخصيص هذه الحرمة باليهود كما أشرنا اليه من وجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet forbade every fanged predator and clawed bird; the Imam calls this solitary report contrary to the Qurʾān and inadmissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r5.anchor: فما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم حرم كل ذي ناب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī closes by flagging an objection to the Imam’s argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p49/r6.anchor: قول الجماعة السابق وفيه نظر لا يخفى فتدبر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r1.claim: Every unsplit-hoofed or unsplit-toed animal is included, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r1.anchor: {حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} وهو ما لم يكن مشقوق الأصابع من البهائم والطير مثل: البعير والنعامة والإوز والبط،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r2.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r2.claim: Al-Qutaybi reports an interpretation covering every clawed bird and every hoofed beast, calling the hoof a nail metaphorically.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r2.anchor: قال القتيبي: هو كل ذي مخلب من الطير وكل ذي حافر من [الدواب] (1)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r3.claim: The forbidden fats are visceral fat, called al-thurub, and kidney fat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r3.anchor: {ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما} يعني شحوم الجوف، وهي الثروب، وشحم الكليتين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r4.claim: The exception includes fat attached to the back and flank from within the animals' bellies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r4.anchor: {إلا ما حملت ظهورهما} أي: إلا ما علق بالظهر والجنب من داخل بطونهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r5.claim: Al-hawaya are the intestines, with singular forms hawiya and hawiya, and the exception covers their fat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r5.anchor: {أو الحوايا} وهي المباعر، واحدتها: حاوية وحوية، أي: ما حملته الحوايا من الشحم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r6.claim: The fat mixed with bone means tail fat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r6.anchor: {أو ما اختلط بعظم} يعني: شحم الألية، هذا كله داخل في الاستثناء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r7.claim: All three exceptions are included; the prohibition is restricted to the omentum and kidney fat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r7.anchor: هذا كله داخل في الاستثناء، والتحريم مختص بالثرب (2) وشحم الكلية.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r8.claim: Jabir reports that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet forbade selling wine, carrion, pork, and idols; when asked about uses for carrion fat, he said it was forbidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r8.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول عام الفتح وهو بمكة "إن الله ورسوله حرم بيع الخمر والميتة والخنزير والأصنام"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r9.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r9.claim: The Prophet said God curse the Jews: when forbidden these fats, they melted them, sold them, and ate their price.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p199#2/r9.anchor: ثم قال رسول الله عند ذلك: "قاتل الله اليهود إن الله عز وجل لما حرم شحومهما جملوه ثم باعوه فأكلوا ثمنه"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r1.claim: The dietary prohibition was punishment for their wrongdoing, including killing prophets, blocking God's path, taking usury, and unlawfully consuming people's property.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r1.anchor: ذلك التحريم عقوبة لهم {ببغيهم} أي: بظلمهم من قتلهم الأنبياء وصدهم عن سبيل الله وأخذهم الربا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r2.claim: God is truthful about what He prohibited for them and about their wrongdoing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p200/r2.anchor: {وإنا لصادقون} في الإخبار عما حرمنا عليهم وعن بغيهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r1.claim: Every possessor of a nail includes camels, wild beasts, and birds; another view includes every clawed or hoofed animal, calling the hoof a nail metaphorically.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r1.anchor: كل ماله أصبع الإبل والسباع والطيور. وقيل كل ذي مخلب وحافر

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r2.claim: The generalization of the prohibition may have been the consequence of their wrongdoing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r2.anchor: ولعل المسبب عن الظلم تعميم التحريم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r3.claim: The forbidden fats include the omenta and kidney fats; the possessive construction strengthens the connection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r3.anchor: الثروب وشحوم الكلى والإضافة لزيادة الربط

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r4.claim: The exception is fat attached to the animals' backs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r5.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the intestines, a plural of ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r5.anchor: أمعاء جمع حاوية، أو حاوياء كقاصعاء وقواصع

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r6.claim: Alternatively, al-ḥawāyā coordinates with 'their fats,' with aw functioning like wāw.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r6.anchor: وقيل هو عطف على شحومهما وأو بمعنى الواو

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r7.claim: What is mixed with bone is the fat of the tail, attached to the coccyx.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r8.claim: That refers either to the prohibition or to the punishment, imposed because of their wrongdoing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r8.anchor: التحريم أو الجزاء. { جزينهم ببغيهم } بسبب ظلمهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:146/r9.claim: God is truthful in what He reports, or in His promise and threat.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r2.claim: This verse answers the claim that God prohibited nothing for the Jews and that Israel alone imposed the restrictions on himself.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r3.claim: Dhū ẓufur covers animals with something like a human finger or claw: camels, predatory beasts, and birds that use their talons.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r3.anchor: على ما هو كالإصبع للآدمي من الإبل والسباع والطيور التي تتقوى بأظفارها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r4.claim: Cattle and sheep, which have cloven hooves, were subject to the prohibition on their fats.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r5.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the coiled, intertwined intestines; Biqāʿī gives ḥawiya as the singular and the pattern faʿāʾil, like safīna and safāʾin, with alternative singular forms.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r5.anchor: وهي الأمعاء التي هي متعاطفة متلوية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r6.claim: Fat carried on the backs, in the intestines, or mixed with bone is exempt; tail fat is an example, and the phrasing indicates other fats of the two species remained lawful.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r6.anchor: وهذا السياق بتقدم الجار وبناء الكلام عليه يدل على أن ما عدا المذكور من الصنفين حلال لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r7.claim: The prohibition of these wholesome foods was a great recompense for the Jews’ transgressions and boundary-crossing.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r7.anchor: التحريم العظيم والجزاء الكبير وهو تحريم الطيبات

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r8.claim: The verse’s detail proves the Prophet’s truth: he knew the prior revelation without contact with Jewish followers, study with scholars, or learning from books.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r8.anchor: بيان اطلاعه صلى الله عليه وسلم على تفصيل ما أوحي إلى من تقدمه ولما يشامم أحدا من أتباعهم ولا دارس عالما ولا درس علما قط

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r9.claim: The juxtaposition honors this community: necessity can make otherwise forbidden foods lawful and remove hardship, whereas some wholesome foods stayed forbidden to the Jews as punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r9.anchor: تفضيله هذه الأمة بأنه أحل لها الخبائث عند الضرورة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r10.claim: The comparison warns this community not to transgress and incur the punishment imposed on earlier people.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p736/r10.anchor: أتم تحذير لهذه الأمة من أن يبغوا فيعاقبوا كما عوقب من قبلهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r1.claim: Biqāʿī connects the warning against transgression with the prohibition in 5:1 on hunting while in consecration.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r1.anchor: فبان الصدق وحصحص الحق ولم يبقى لمتعنت كلام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r2.claim: God’s truth is constant from eternity to eternity, as befits His majesty; the proof leaves no room for obstinate objection.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p737/r2.anchor: ثابت صدقنا أزلا وأبدا كما اقتضاه ما لنا من العظمة

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r1.claim: The restriction applies specifically to the Jews, not to other peoples, past or future.
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r1.anchor: {وعلى الذين هادوا} أي : على اليهود خاصة لا على من عداهم

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r2.claim: Dhi ẓufur includes any animal with toes, whether its digits are split, like predators, dogs, and cats, or unsplit, like camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r2.anchor: كل ما له أصبع سواء كان ما بين أصابعه منفرجا كأنواع السباع والكلاب والسنانير

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r3.claim: Some clawed animals had once been lawful to them; after their wrongdoing the prohibition covered all such animals.
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r3.anchor: وكان بعض ذوات الظفر حلالا لهم فلما ظلموا عم التحريم

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r4.claim: The phrase concerns the prohibition of cattle and sheep fats, not their meat, which remains lawful.
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r4.anchor: {ومن البقر والغنم} متعلق بقوله : {حرمنا عليهم شحومهمآ} لا لحومهما

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r5.claim: The prohibited fats are the omentum and kidney fats.

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r6.claim: The exception includes fat carried along the backs and sides, from the shoulders to the hips, inside and out.
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r6.anchor: أي : إلا ما اشتملت على الظهور والجنوب من شحم الكتفين إلى الوركين

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r7.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is coordinated with the preceding exception and refers to what the intestines carry and surround.
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r7.anchor: {أو الحوايآ} عطف على ظهورهما ، أي : أو إلا الذي حملته الأمعاء

BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#2/r8.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is the plural of ḥawiyya, defined in al-Ṣiḥāḥ as the intestines and bowels.

BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r1.claim: This includes tail fat attached to the coccyx, the tailbone; the text says this bone is the first created and last to decay.
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r1.anchor: {أو ما اختلط بعظم} عطف على ما حملت وهو شحم الألية

BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r2.claim: The source reports the claim that the coccyx is the first bone created and the last to decay.
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r2.anchor: ويقال إنه أول ما يخلق وآخر ما يبلى

BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r3.claim: The prohibition was punishment for the Jews' wrongdoing, including unjustly killing prophets, taking usury, and consuming people's wealth unlawfully.
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r3.anchor: {ببغيهم} أي : بسبب ظلمهم وهو قتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق

BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r4.claim: Each new sin brought a further ban on something previously lawful; Jews denied this and claimed those things had always been forbidden to earlier peoples.
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r4.anchor: وكانوا كلما أتوا بمعصية عوقبوا بتحريم شيء مما أحل لهم

BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r5.claim: God affirms His truthfulness, especially in reporting the prohibition and the Jews' wrongdoing.
BURSEVI:v3p88#3/r5.anchor: أي : في الإخبار عن كل شيء لا سيما في الإخبار عن التحريم المذكور

DURR-FULL:v3p376/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas defines every animal with a claw here as one whose toes are not split, including camels and ostriches.
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} قال: هو الذي ليس بمنفرج الأصابع يعني ليس بمشقوق الأصابع منها الإبل والنعام

DURR-FULL:v3p376/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r7.claim: In another report Ibn Abbas identifies the animals with an un split hoof as the camel and ostrich.
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} قال: هو البعير والنعامة

DURR-FULL:v3p376/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r8.claim: Qatada reports the view that the category includes camels, ostriches, and certain birds and fish.
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r8.anchor: عن قتادة {حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} قال: كان يقال: هو البعير والنعامة في أشياء من الطير والحيتان

DURR-FULL:v3p376/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r9.claim: Mujahid says Jews ate animals with split feet, such as chickens and sparrows, but not camels, ostriches, al-warīna, or wild asses, whose feet are not split.
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد {حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} قال: كل شيء لم تفرج قوائمه من البهائم وما انفرج أكلته اليهود

DURR-FULL:v3p376/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r10.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr includes the rooster among the animals forbidden to the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} قال: الديك منه

DURR-FULL:v3p376/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the same split-foot distinction and says Jews ate split-footed animals but not camel, ostrich, duck, goose, or wild ass.
DURR-FULL:v3p376/r11.anchor: عن ابن جريج {حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} قال: كل شيء لم تفرج قوائمه من البهائم وما انفرجت قوائمه أكلوه

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet condemning Jews who melted prohibited animal fat, sold it, and consumed the proceeds.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: قاتل الله اليهود لما حرم الله عليهم شحومها جملوه ثم باعوه فأكلوها

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r2.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r2.claim: Usama ibn Zayd reports the Prophet cursing Jews who sold prohibited fat and ate its price.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r2.anchor: عن أسامة بن زيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن الله اليهود حرمت عليهم الشحوم فباعوها وأكلوا أثمانها

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r3.claim: Umar reports the Prophet cursing Jews for selling prohibited fat and consuming its proceeds.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن الله اليهود حرمت عليهم الشحوم فباعوها وأكلوا أثمانها

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet condemning Jews for selling the fat God had prohibited and eating its price.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاتل الله اليهود حرم الله عليهم الشحوم فباعوها وأكلوا ثمنها

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that God prohibited the Jews from fat, so they sold it and ate its price; he adds that whatever God forbids a people to eat, He also forbids its price.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لعن الله اليهود ثلاثا إن الله حرم عليهم الشحوم

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the exception as fat attached to the animals' backs.
