DURR-FULL:v3p378/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما} يعني ما علق بالظهر من الشحم

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-ḥawāyā as the mabʿar, the bowel or place of excretion.

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the prohibited fats were the omentum and kidney fat.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r8.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما} قال: حرم الله عليهم الثرب وشحم الكليتين

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says only the omentum, kidney fat, and fat not attached to bone were prohibited.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: إنما حرم عليهم الثرب وشحم الكلية وكل شحم كان ليس في عظم

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r10.claim: Abu Salih identifies the back-carried exception as tail fat, al-ḥawāyā as the mabʿar, and the bone-mixed exception as fat.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله {إلا ما حملت ظهورهما} قال: الإلية {أو الحوايا} قال: المبعر

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses al-ḥawāyā as the bowels or intestines.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أو الحوايا} قال: المباعر

DURR-FULL:v3p378/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r12.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak explains al-ḥawāyā as the animal's resting places and bowels, and bone-mixed fat as fat adhering to bone.
DURR-FULL:v3p378/r12.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {أو الحوايا} قال: المرابض والمباعر {أو ما اختلط بعظم} قال: ما ألزق بالعظم

DURR-FULL:v3p379/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd defines al-ḥawāyā as the intestinal folds or pens where the intestines lie centrally, called marābiḍ in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r1.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: الحوايا المرابض التي تكون فيها الامعاء تكون وسطها وهي بنات اللبن

DURR-FULL:v3p379/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says tail fat mixed with the coccyx is lawful, as are fats of the limbs, flank, head, eye, and ear when regarded as mixed with bone; only omentum and kidney fat and other fat not in bone were forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أو ما اختلط بعظم} قال: الإلية اختلط شحم الالية بالعصعص فهو حلال

DURR-FULL:v3p379/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r3.claim: Qatada says God imposed these restrictions as punishment for the Jews' transgression, not because the foods were impure.
DURR-FULL:v3p379/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم} قال: إنما حرم الله ذلك عليهم عقوبة ببغيهم فشدد عليهم بذلك وما هو بخبيث

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r1.claim: Mujahid associates the Jews' restriction with their observance of the Sabbath.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : تهودت اليهود السبت قوله : حرمنا كل ذي ظفر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r2.claim: He defines an animal with a claw here as one without split toes, including camels and ostriches.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر ، قال : هو الذي ليس بمنفرد الاصابع

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك وعطاء الخراساني ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r3.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same definition of animals without split toes.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r3.anchor: وروى عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك وعطاء الخراساني ومقاتل بن حيان

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r4.speaker: حنش الصنعاني
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r4.claim: He adds the pig to the animals covered by the prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r4.anchor: عن حنش الصنعاني وزاد فيه : والخنزير

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r5.speaker: السدي وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r5.claim: They add the goose to the animals covered by the prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r5.anchor: عن السدى وقتادة وزاد فيه : والوز

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r6.claim: He adds the rooster to the animals covered by the prohibition.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r7.claim: He identifies the forbidden fats as the omentum and kidney fat, and says the Jews claimed Israel had forbidden it, so they forbade it too.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r7.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عيهم شحومهما قال : حرمنا عليهم من الشحوم الثرب وشحم الكليتين

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r8.claim: He means fat attached to the animals' backs; al-Dahhak and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : الا ما حملت ظهورهما يعني : ما علق بالظهر من الشحم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r9.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r9.claim: He glosses the fat carried on the backs as the tail fat; al-Sadi is reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r9.anchor: عن أبي صالح : الا ما حملت ظهورهما قال : الالية

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r10.claim: He glosses al-ḥawāyā as the animal's bowel or dung-bearing parts; several other authorities are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : أو الحوايا هو المبعر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r11.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r11.claim: He glosses al-ḥawāyā as the bowels and resting places.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1409#2/r11.anchor: عن جويبر عن الضحاك : أو الحوايا قال : المباعر والمرابض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r1.claim: He defines al-ḥawāyā as the animal's central abdominal folds containing the intestines, called marābiḍ in Arabic; he also calls them “banāt al-laban.”
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r1.anchor: ابن زيد ، في قوله : أو الحوايا قال : الحوايا المرابض التي تكون فيها الامعاء ، تكون وسطها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r2.claim: In another report he takes al-ḥawāyā as the bellies, excluding the fatty caul; Muqatil ibn Hayyan is reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r2.anchor: عن علي بن الحكم عن الضحاك : اما قوله : أو الحوايا فالبطون غير الثروب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r3.speaker: عبيد بن سلمان عن الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r3.claim: A report through ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman gives the contrary distinction: the fatty caul is outside the bellies.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r3.anchor: وخالفه عبيد بن سلمان عن الضحاك فقال : يعني بالثروب : غير البطون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r4.claim: He explains what is mixed with bone as fat; al-Sadi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are also reported to give this gloss, with al-Sadi specifying fat on bone.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح : أو ما اختلط بعظم قال : الشحم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r5.claim: He explains the phrase as fat attached to bone.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك : أو ما اختلط بعظم قال : ما الزق بالعظم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r6.claim: He says these foods were forbidden as punishment for the Jews' transgression.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r6.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله : ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم ، انما حرم ذلك عليهم ، عقوبة ببغيهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r7.claim: He links the punishment to their invoking an oath about what God had forbidden them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1411/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قوله : ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم يقول : باستحلافهم ما كان الله حرم عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r1.claim: The report of Jewish dietary restrictions is coordinated with the command in 6:145: explain what Islam forbids, then recall the separate restrictions once imposed on Jews.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r1.anchor: جملة : { وعلى الذين ادوا حرمنا } عطف على جملة : { قل } ( الأنعام : 145 ) عطف خبر على إنشاء ، أي بين لهم ما حرم في الإسلام ، واذكر لهم ما حرمنا على الذين هادوا قبل الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r2.claim: The surrounding discussion distinguishes impure foods from offerings to other than God; the Jewish restrictions are added as temporary rules for a particular wisdom, showing that invented pagan taboos were never God's law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r2.anchor: أعقب ذلك بذكر ما حرمه على بني إسرائيل تحريما خاصا لحكمة خاصة بأحوالهم ، وموقتة إلى مجيء الشريعة الخاتمة . والمقصود من ذكر هذا الأخير : أن يظهر للمشركين أن ما حرموه ليس من تشريع الله في الحال ولا فيما مضى ، فهو ضلال بحت .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r3.claim: Fronting “upon those who Judaized” marks the restriction as exclusive to them and not other communities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r3.anchor: وتقديم المجرور على متعلقة في قوله : { وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا } لإفادة الاختصاص ، أي عليهم لا على غيرهم من الأمم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r4.claim: Dhufr is the nail or claw at the ends of human and animal digits under the skin, contrasted with hoof and cloven hoof; it includes camels, predators, dogs, cats, rabbits, and hyraxes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r4.anchor: والظفر : العظم الذي تحت الجلد في منتهى أصابع الإنسان والحيوان والمخالب ، وهو يقابل الحافر والظلف ويكون للإبل والسبع والكلب والهر والأرنب والوبر ونحوها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r5.claim: Moses' law prohibited these animals to Jews; Deuteronomy 14 is cited as forbidding camel, hare, and hyrax.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r5.anchor: فهذه محرمة على اليهود بنص شريعة موسى عليه السلام ففي الإصحاح الرابع عشر من سفر التثنية : ( الجمل والأرنب والوبر فلا تأكلوها ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r6.claim: Shuḥūm means the fatty tissue associated with an animal's meat; Jews could eat cattle and sheep but not their fat, except that on their backs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r6.anchor: والشحوم : جمع شحم ، وهو المادة الدهنية التي تكون مع اللحم في جسد الحيوان ، وقد أباح الله لليهود أكل لحوم البقر والغنم وحرم عليهم شحومهما إلا ما كان في الظهر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r7.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is coordinated with the backs, so the exception concerns fat borne by the surrounding sacs, not the prohibited category; ḥawāyā is plural of ḥawiyya.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p141/r7.anchor: و { الحوايا } معطوف على { ظهورهما } . فالمقصود العطف على المباح لا على المحرم ، أي : أو ما حملت الحوايا ، وهي جمع حوية ، وهي الأكياس الشحمية التي تحوي الأمعاء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r1.claim: Fat wrapped around an animal's bone because of its fatness is permitted as an exception, since separating it from the bone is difficult.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r1.anchor: { أو ما اختلط بعظم } هو الشحم الذي يكون ملتفا على عظم الحيوان من السمن فهو معفو عنه لعسر تجريده عن عظمه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r2.claim: These restrictions appear to be Mosaic and differ from 4:160's later prohibitions, since the offenses listed there arose after Moses; the present punishment relates to transgressions during the wilderness period.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الشحوم كانت محرمة عليهم بشريعة موسى عليه السلام ، فهي غير المحرمات التي أجملتها آية سورة النساء ( 160 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r3.claim: The transgressions included refusing to endure one food, refusing to fight, and worshipping the calf; the Qur'an recounts many of these in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r3.anchor: في مدة التيه ، مما أخبر الله به عنهم : مثل قولهم : { لن نصبر على طعام واحد } ( البقرة : 61 ) وقولهم : { فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا } ( المائدة : 24 ) وعبادتهم العجل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r4.claim: Their transgression arose from hard dispositions and dominance of animal over angelic power; perhaps the prohibition eased that hardness, while its contrast displays God's grace in allowing Muslims animals not forbidden by Qur'an or accepted Sunnah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r4.anchor: ومناسبة تحريم هذه المحرمات للكون جزاء لبغيهم : أن بغيهم نشأ عن صلابة نفوسهم وتغلب القوة الحيوانية فيهم على القوة الملكية ، فلعل الله حرم عليهم هذه الأمور تخفيفا من صلابتهم ، وفي ذلك إظهار منته على المسلمين بإباحة جميع الحيوان لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r5.claim: Pork is omitted although the Torah forbids it because this passage treats restrictions distinctive to Jews that were temporary, not prohibitions that also apply in Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r5.anchor: ولم يذكر الله تحريم لحم الخنزير ، مع أنه مما شمله نص التوراة ، لأنه إنما ذكر هنا ما خصوا بتحريمه مما لم يحرم في الإسلام ، أي ما كان تحريمه موقتا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r6.claim: The fronted phrase about cattle and sheep emphasizes that restriction, which readers would anticipate after hearing that every nail-bearing animal was forbidden; it works like opening with “as for.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r6.anchor: وتقديم المجرور على عامله في قوله : { ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم } للاهتمام ببيان ذلك ، لأنه مما يلتفت الذهن إليه عند سماع تحريم كل ذي ظفر فيترقب الحكم بالنسبة إليهما فتقديم المجرور بمنزلة الافتتاح ب ( أما ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r7.claim: The closing clause summarizes the reason for the restrictions: the demonstrative refers to the prohibition expressed by “We prohibited.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r7.anchor: وجملة : { ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم } تذييل يبين علة تحريم ما حرم عليهم . واسم الإشارة في قوله : { ذلك جزيناهم } مقصود به التحريم المأخوذ من قوله : { حرمنا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r8.claim: The demonstrative is the second object of “We requited them”; it precedes the verb and first object to emphasize and confirm that prohibition was requital for their transgression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p142/r8.anchor: فهو في موضع مفعول ثان : ل { جزيناهم } قدم على عامله ومفعوله الأول للاهتمام به والتثبيت على أن التحريم جزاء لبغيهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r1.claim: The closing assertion confirms that God truly imposed these prohibitions on the Jews and refutes their denial that they were divine punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r1.anchor: وجملة : { وإنا لصادقون } تذييل للجملة التي قبلها قصدا لتحقيق أن الله حرم عليهم ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r2.claim: The Jews wrongly attributed these restrictions to Jacob: he only forbade himself camel meat and milk, and a personal vow or bodily benefit did not bind his descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r2.anchor: وليس قولهم بحق : لأن يعقوب إنما حرم على نفسه لحوم الإبل وألبانها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur links the emphatic rebuttal to the challenge in 3:93–95: the prohibitions were written in the Torah, so the Jews could not deny them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p144/r3.anchor: وأن هذه الأشياء التي ذكر الله تحريمها على بني إسرائيل مذكور تحريمها في التوراة فكيف ينكرون تحريمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r1.claim: After prohibitions for Muḥammad's community, Jewish prohibitions refute their claim God forbade nothing and Israel chose the restrictions; hādū and Jews were discussed in al-Baqara.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r1.anchor: لما ذكر الله عز وجل ما حرم على أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أعقب ذلك بذكر ما حرم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r2.claim: Dhi ẓufur includes camels, ostriches, geese, and similar animals with unsplit toes and nails. Abu Zayd restricts it to camels, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects; Thaʿlab's predator/non-predator distinction fails because lions have nails.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r2.anchor: وكل ذي ظفر يراد به الإبل والنعام والإوز ونحوه من الحيوان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور والحسن والأعرج وأبو السمال قعنب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r3.claim: The majority have ḍamma on both consonants; al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj have still fāʾ; Abu al-Sammāl Quʿnub has kasra on ẓāʾ and still fāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ظفر» بضم الظاء والفاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r4.claim: Forbidden fats include caul fat, kidney fat, and pure fat except what the verse exempts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r4.anchor: وهي الثروب وشحم الكلى وما كان شحما خالصا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r5.speaker: ابن المنذر عن مالك وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports in al-Ishrāf that Mālik and others prohibit fat from Jewish slaughter; this is the apparent Mudawwana ruling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r5.anchor: فحكى ابن المنذر في الأشراف عن مالك وغيره منع أكل الشحم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r6.claim: On the view that ‘food of the People of Scripture’ in 5:5 means meat from their slaughter, what they cannot eat receives no valid slaughter and is like blood in Muslim slaughter; thus a Jew's camel or rabbit is not eaten.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r6.anchor: وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم [المائدة: 5] بأنه المطعوم من ذبائحهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r7.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r7.claim: Another report says Mālik merely disliked fat from People of Scripture, not that he prohibited it; some permit such fat and their slaughter of animals forbidden to them when commissioned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p357#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن مالك رحمه الله كراهية الشحم من ذبائح أهل الكتاب دون تحريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r1.claim: Reading 5:5 as referring only to slaughter makes food mean slaughter alone, detached from food eaten by the People of the Book; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this strained and weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r1.anchor: وهذا قول ضعيف لأنه جرد لفظة وطعام من معنى أن تكون مطعوما لأهل الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r2.claim: Some prohibited the method or route under discussion, some disliked it, and some permitted it; Malik initially eased it in al-Mudawwana, then returned to prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r2.anchor: وأما الطريق فحرمه قوم وكرهه قوم وأباحه قوم وخففه مالك في المدونة ثم رجع إلى منعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r3.speaker: ابن حبيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r3.claim: Ibn Habib says Jewish slaughter is impermissible for us when our Scripture confirms the prohibition; a prohibition known only from their statements does not make their slaughter forbidden to us.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r3.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب ما كان محرما عليهم وعلمنا ذلك من كتابنا فلا يحل لنا من ذبائحهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r4.claim: The exception for what the backs carry refers to fat mixed with flesh in the back, flanks, and similar places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r4.anchor: يريد ما اختلط باللحم في الظهر والأجناب ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r5.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r5.claim: Al-Suddi and Abu Salih include the tails among what the backs carry or among the hawaya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r5.anchor: قال السدي وأبو صالح: الأليات مما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r6.claim: Hawaya has three proposed plural formations: from ḥawiyya, ḥāwiya, or ḥāwiyāʾ, yielding the stated faʿāʾil or fawāʿil patterns.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r6.anchor: قال هو جمع حوية على وزن فعلية، فوزن «حوايا» على هذا فعائل كسفينة وسفائن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r7.claim: On the first derivation, ḥawāyā began as ḥawāyī, with the final yāʾ changed to alif, opening the hamza, which was then replaced by yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r7.anchor: وأما «الحوايا» على الوزن الأول فأصلها حوايي فقلب الياء الأخيرة ألفا فانفتحت لذلك الهمزة ثم بدلت ياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r8.claim: On the latter two derivations, the original form was ḥawāwī and the second wāw was replaced by hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r8.anchor: وأما على الوزنين الأخيرين فأصل «حوايا» حواوي وبدلت الواو الثانية همزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r9.claim: A ḥawiyya is something curled and rounded inside the belly, such as the intestines, viscera, and related contents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r9.anchor: والحوية ما تحوى في البطن واستدار وهي المصارين والحشوة ونحوهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن عباس والسدي وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r10.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd identify the hawaya as the bowels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة وابن عباس والسدي وابن زيد: «الحوايا» المباعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r11.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r11.claim: Some say the hawaya are the supports or folds containing the intestines, identified as the milk-bearing parts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هي المرابط التي تكون فيها الأمعاء وهي بنات اللبن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r12.claim: What is mixed with bone means fat found throughout the rest of the animal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r13.claim: Hawaya is coordinated with mā in the exception phrase, so it is accusative as a coordinate of the word governed by the exception.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r13.anchor: والحوايا معطوف على ما في قوله إلا ما حملت فهي في موضع نصب عطفا على المنصوب بالاستثناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r14.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r14.claim: Al-Kisaʾi instead coordinates hawaya with backs, construing the phrase as what the backs or hawaya carry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r14.anchor: وقال الكسائي الحوايا معطوف على الظهور، كأنه قال «إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو حملت الحوايا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r15.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r15.claim: Some coordinate hawaya with the forbidden fats, which would include it in the prohibition; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as opposed by both wording and sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r15.anchor: وقال بعض الناس الحوايا معطوف على الشحوم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r16.claim: The demonstrative dhālika is nominative in the sentence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r16.anchor: ذلك في موضع رفع وجزيناهم ببغيهم يقتضي أن هذا التحريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r17.claim: The prohibitions were requital for the Jews’ sins, transgression, and disobedience to the prophets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r17.anchor: إنما كان عقوبة لهم على ذنوبهم وبغيهم واستعصائهم على الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r18.claim: God's assertion of truth implicitly charges the Jews with lying when they claimed God prohibited nothing and that they only followed what Israel had forbidden himself; it refutes them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p358/r18.anchor: يتضمن التعريض بكذبهم في قولهم ما حرم الله علينا شيئا وإنما اقتدينا بإسرائيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r1.speaker: الحسن، الأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Aʿmash read zufr with a still fāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعمش ظفر بسكون الفاء وهذا التحريم تحريم بلوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r2.claim: This prohibition is a trial and a punishment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، مجاهد، قتادة، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r3.claim: One view defines any animal with a nail as one whose toes are not split, including camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r3.anchor: أنه ما ليس بمنفرج الأصابع كالإبل والنعام والإوز والبط قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r4.claim: A second view limits the prohibited animal to camels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r4.anchor: والثاني الإبل فقط قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r5.claim: A third view includes every hoofed beast and clawed bird; Ibn Qutayba says hoof is metaphorically called a nail, as Arabs use hooves for feet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r5.anchor: والثالث كل ذي حافر من الدواب ومخلب من الطير قاله ابن قتيبة قال وسمى الحافر ظفرا على الإستعارة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r6.speaker: شاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r6.claim: An anonymous poem uses the phrase hooves that are not split to mean feet, although hooves properly belong to sheep and cattle.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r6.anchor: وأنشدوا سأمنعها أو سوف أجعل أمرها إلى ملك أظلافه لم تشقق أراد قدميه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari lists three forms for zufr: zufr, zufr, and aẓfur.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r7.anchor: قال ابن الانباري الظفر هاهنا يجري مجرى الظفر للانسان وفيه ثلاث لغات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r8.speaker: شعراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r8.claim: Three further anonymous lines use zufr and aẓfur for a nail or claw, as in the expressions winged and clawed, a fang and nail, and a measured aẓfur.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r8.anchor: وقال الشاعر ألم تر أن الموت أدرك من مضى فلم يبق منه ذا جناح وذا ظفر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r9.claim: One view says only the caul fat of cattle and sheep was prohibited.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r9.anchor: أحدها أنه إنما حرم من ذلك شحوم الثروب خاصة قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r10.speaker: السدي، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r10.claim: A second view includes both caul fat and kidney fat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r10.anchor: والثاني شحوم الثروب والكلى قاله السدي وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r11.claim: A third view includes all fat that is neither mixed with bone nor on a bone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r11.anchor: والثالث كل شحم لم يكن مختلطا بعظم ولا على عظم قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r12.claim: One view takes the exception to mean fat attached to the back.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r12.anchor: أحدها أنه ما علق بالظهر من الشحوم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r13.speaker: أبو صالح، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r13.claim: A second view takes the exception as the tail fat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r13.anchor: والثاني الألية قاله أبو صالح والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r14.claim: A third view takes it as fat attached to the back and side inside the belly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r14.anchor: والثالث ما علق بالظهر والجنب من داخل بطونهما قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r15.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، ابن جبير، مجاهد، قتادة، السدي، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r15.claim: These authorities identify al-hawaya as the intestines or entrails (al-mabaʿir).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r15.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن وابن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن قتيبة هي المباعر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r16.speaker: ابن زيد، الفراء، الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r16.claim: Other explanations call them the milk-bearing glands and the places holding the intestines; al-Asmaʿi gives singular forms hawiya, hāwiya, and ḥawiya.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p141/r16.anchor: وقال ابن زيد هي بنات اللبن وهي المرابض التي تكون فيها الأمعاء وقال الفراء الحوايا هي المباعر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r1.speaker: شاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r1.claim: Two anonymous poetic lines cite hawiya and hawāyih as usages of the word for the body's viscera.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r1.anchor: قال الشاعر أقتلهم ولا أرى معاوية الجاحظ العين العظيم الحاوية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r2.claim: Abu ʿUbayda defines hawaya as what folds within the belly; al-Zajjaj says it collectively names the gathered, curved contents, including the milk glands, intestines, and their compartments.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة الحوايا ما تحوي من البطن أي ما استدار منها وقال الزجاج الحوايا اسم لجميع ما تحوي من البطن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r3.claim: One view says the phrase includes abdominal fat and tail fat, because they lie on bones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه شحم البطن والالية لأنهما على عظم قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r4.claim: A second view includes fat in the limbs, side, head, eyes, and ears, all of which is mixed with bone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r4.anchor: والثاني كل شحم في القوائم والجنب والرأس والعينين والأذنين فهو مما اختلط بعظم قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r5.claim: Exegetes agree that the fat carried on the backs is lawful under the exception.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r5.anchor: واتفقوا على أن ما حملت ظهورها حلال بالاستثناء من التحريم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r6.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r6.claim: Most exegetes include fat carried by the hawaya and fat mixed with bone in the exception, making it permissible.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r6.anchor: أحدهما أنه داخل في الاستثناء فهو مباح والمعنى وأبيح لهم ما حملت الحوايا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead coordinates the hawaya and bone-mixed fat with the prohibited fats, not with the exception; only back fat is exempt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه نسق على ما حرم لا على الاستثناء فالمعنى حرمنا عليهم شحومهما أو الحوايا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r8.claim: Here aw functions as wa, as in 76:24.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p143/r8.anchor: فأما أو المذكورة هاهنا فهي بمعنى الواو كقوله ﴿ آثما أو كفورا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r1.claim: The prohibition was punishment for their transgression.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r1.anchor: أي ذلك التحريم عقوبة لهم على بغيهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r2.claim: One explanation of their transgression is their killing of prophets and consuming usury.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه قتلهم الأنبياء وأكلهم الربا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r3.claim: A second explanation is that they prohibited what had been made lawful for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p144/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه تحريم ما أحل لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir defines creatures with an undivided claw or toe as livestock and birds whose digits are not split, including camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.anchor: وهو البهائم والطير ما لم يكن مشقوق الأصابع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة ومجاهد والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and one report from al-Suddi identify the prohibited animals as camels and ostriches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} وهو البعير والنعامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr first defines the category as animals without separated toes; in another report he includes all creatures with separated toes, such as a rooster.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو الذي ليس بمنفرج الأصابع، وفي رواية عنه: كل شيء متفرق الأصابع، ومنه الديك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.claim: Qatada says it includes camels, ostriches, and some birds and fish; another report lists camels, ostriches, ducks, and creatures whose toes are not split.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} وكان يقال: البعير والنعامة وأشياء من الطير والحيتان. وفي رواية:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج عن مجاهد والقاسم بن أبي بزة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports Mujahid’s examples of camel and ostrich; Qasim ibn Abi Bizza explains the phrase as animals whose feet do not separate, which Jews could not eat, including wild asses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: عن مجاهد: {كل ذي ظفر} قال: النعامة والبعير، شقا شقا. قلت للقاسم بن أبي بزة وحدثنيه: ما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r1.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r1.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the forbidden fats as the omentum and kidney fat; Jews claimed Israel had prohibited it for himself, and Ibn Zayd gives the same explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r1.anchor: قال السدي: [يعني] (1) الثرب وشحم الكليتين. وكانت اليهود تقول (2) : إنه حرمه إسرائيل فنحن نحرمه. وكذا قال ابن زيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r2.claim: Qatada defines the fats as the omentum and any similar fat that is not within a bone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: الثرب وكل شحم (3) كان كذلك ليس في عظم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the exception as fat attached to the backs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {إلا ما حملت ظهورهما} يعني: ما علق بالظهر من الشحوم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r4.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r4.claim: Al-Suddi and Abu Salih identify the fat carried on the backs as tail fat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r4.anchor: وقال السدي وأبو صالح: الألية، مما (4) حملت ظهورهما.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir says hawaya is the plural of hawya, hawiyah, or huwiyya: the folded, gathered, rounded part of the belly, including milk glands, abomasums, resting places, and intestines.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r5.anchor: قال الإمام أبو جعفر بن جرير: {الحوايا} جمع، واحدها حاوياء، وحاوية وحوية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir construes the exception as the fats carried by the backs or carried by the hawaya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r6.anchor: ومعنى الكلام: ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما، إلا ما حملت ظهورهما، أو ما حملت الحوايا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r7.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the hawaya as the abomasum or entrail region.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {أو الحوايا} وهي المبعر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r8.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك وقتادة وأبو مالك والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r8.claim: Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Qatada, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi gloss hawaya as the abomasum and resting place.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {الحوايا} المبعر، والمربض. وكذا قال سعيد بن جبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r9.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says hawaya are the resting places around the central intestines, called milk glands or marabid in Arabic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355/r9.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: {الحوايا} المرابض التي تكون فيها الأمعاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r1.claim: Fat mixed with bones was also made lawful to the Jews.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r1.anchor: أي: وإلا ما اختلط من الشحوم بالعظام فقد أحللناه لهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says tail fat mixed with the coccyx is lawful; fat in the limbs, flank, head, and eye, and whatever mixes with bone, is also lawful, as al-Suddi similarly says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: شحم الألية اختلط بالعصعص، فهو حلال. وكل شيء في القوائم والجنب والرأس والعين وما اختلط بعظم، فهو حلال، ونحوه قال (7) السدي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r3.claim: The restrictions were imposed as requital for the Jews’ wrongdoing and disobedience to God’s commands, as also stated in 4:160.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r3.anchor: هذا التضييق إنما فعلناه بهم وألزمناهم (8) به، مجازاة لهم على بغيهم ومخالفتهم أوامرنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r4.claim: God is just in the recompense imposed on them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r4.anchor: أي: وإنا لعادلون فيما جزيناهم به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir says God truthfully informed Muhammad that He prohibited these fats for the Jews, contrary to their claim that Israel had prohibited them for himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: وإنا لصادقون فيما أخبرناك به يا محمد من تحريمنا ذلك عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that when ʿUmar heard Samura had sold wine, he condemned him and cited the Prophet’s report about Jews processing prohibited fat to sell it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عباس: بلغ عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، أن سمرة باع خمرا، فقال: قاتل الله سمرة!

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r7.claim: Jabir reports that in the year of the Conquest the Prophet prohibited selling wine, carrion, pork, and idols; he ruled dead-animal fats unlawful despite their uses, recalling that Jews processed and sold forbidden fat. The report is transmitted by the major hadith collectors.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r7.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول عام الفتح: "إن الله ورسوله حرم بيع الخمر والميتة والخنزير والأصنام".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet condemning Jews for selling prohibited fats and consuming the proceeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p355#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r1.claim: Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmit Abu Hurayra’s report that the Prophet condemned Jews for selling forbidden fats and eating their price.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r1.anchor: ورواه البخاري ومسلم جميعا، عن عبدان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r2.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports Ibn ʿAbbas’s account of the Prophet, seated behind the Station, thrice cursing Jews for selling prohibited fat and saying that forbidding food also forbids its price.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان قاعدا خلف المقام، فرفع بصره إلى السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r3.claim: Ahmad and Abu Dawud transmit Ibn ʿAbbas’s report of the Prophet facing the Black Stone, cursing Jews for selling forbidden fats and stating that a forbidden food’s price is forbidden too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r3.anchor: أنبأنا ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاعدا في المسجد مستقبلا الحجر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أسامة بن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r4.claim: Usama ibn Zayd reports that during a visit to the sick Prophet, he condemned Jews who prohibited sheep fat but consumed its sale price; another wording says they sold the forbidden fats and ate their proceeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p356/r4.anchor: عن أسامة بن زيد قال: دخلنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو مريض نعوده

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r1.speaker: عامة القراء
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r1.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on both consonants of ẓufur; al-Ḥasan has kasra on ẓāʾ and sukūn on fāʾ, and Ibn al-Sammāl kasra on both; all are dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: ظفر بضم الظاء والفاء، وعن الحسن بكسر الظاء وسكون الفاء

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r2.claim: Ẓufr is a human or animal nail or claw; the verb can mean inserting one's nail into something, and aẓfar describes long nails.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r2.anchor: الظفر: ظفر الإنسان وغيره، وظفر في الشيء إذا جعل ظفره فيه

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r3.claim: A person called kalīl al-ẓufr is lowly or contemptible.

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses ḥawāyā as the internal organs and lists several possible singular forms, with different morphological patterns.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r4.anchor: الحوايا: المباعر، قال الزجاج: قيل في واحدها حاوية وحاوياء وحوية

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r5.claim: The word describes what gathers and rounds in the belly; ḥiwāʾ can also name a cluster of tents by water.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r5.anchor: وهو ما يحوي في البطن فاجتمع واستدار، والحواء بيوت مجتمعة على ماء

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r6.claim: A cited hadith uses ḥawiyya for a cloak arranged around the camel's hump as a seat.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r6.anchor: ومنه الحديث: كان يحوي وراءه بعباءة ثم يردفها وصفته أن يجعل حوية

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r8.claim: Mā ḥamalat is accusative as an exception.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r8.anchor: إلا ما حملت نصب على الاستثناء

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r9.claim: One parsing makes al-ḥawāyā nominative, coordinated with al-ẓuhūr, with an implied 'or what the viscera carried.'
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r9.anchor: الأول: رفع بالعطف على الظهور بتقدير أو حملت الحوايا

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r10.claim: Another parsing makes al-ḥawāyā accusative, coordinated with the first mā in the exception, with an implied 'I except the viscera.'
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r10.anchor: الثاني: نصب بالعطف على (ما) في إلا ما حملت على تقدير: أستثني ما حملت، وأستثني الحوايا

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r11.claim: Mā ikhtalaṭa is accusative by coordination with the first mā in the exception.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r11.anchor: فأما (ما اختلط) فنصب بالعطف على (ما) الأولى

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r12.claim: It is said Arabs claimed they had learned the ban on the saʾiba from the People of the Book; God denied this and clarified what He had forbidden the Jews.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r12.anchor: قيل: إن العرب قالوا: إنا علمنا تحريم السائبة من أهل الكتاب

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والسدي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r13.claim: These authorities say 'every claw' means animals without split toes, including camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the phrase to camels.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو الإبل فقط، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r15.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r15.claim: Abū ʿAlī includes predators, dogs, cats, and anything that hunts with its claw.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: يدخل فيه جميع السباع والكلاب والسنانير

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r16.speaker: القتبي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r16.claim: Al-Qutbī extends the category to every clawed bird and every hoofed animal.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r16.anchor: وكل ذي مخلب من الطير، وكل ذي حافر من الدواب حكاه [القتبي]

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r17.claim: God forbade the Jews the fat of cattle and sheep except what was carried on their backs, in the viscera, or mixed with bone.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r17.anchor: يعني: وحرمنا شحوم البقر والغنم على اليهود إلا ما استثني، وهو ما حملت الظهور

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r18.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والسدي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r18.claim: These authorities explain al-ḥawāyā as the digestive organs.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r18.anchor: قيل: المباعر، عن ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r19.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r19.claim: Abū ʿAlī instead explains al-ḥawāyā as intestines with fat on them.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r19.anchor: وقيل: الأمعاء التي عليها الشحم، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r20.speaker: ابن جريج والسدي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r20.claim: Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddī identify the fat mixed with bone as flank fat and rump fat over the coccyx.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r20.anchor: قيل: شحم الجنب والألية؛ لأنها على العصعص، عن ابن جريج والسدي

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r21.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r21.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the rump fat is not included in the exception, apparently because he does not count the coccyx as the relevant bone.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r21.anchor: وقيل: الألية لا تدخل في الاستثناء، عن أبي علي كأنه لم يعتد بالعصعص

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r22.claim: These dietary restrictions were imposed as requital for prior transgression, committing prohibitions, and seeking what was not theirs.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r22.anchor: يعني أن هذا التحريم على اليهود كان بسبب تقدم منهم، من ارتكابهم المحظورات والبغي

JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r23.claim: God is truthful about the prohibition; disbelievers falsely attributed their claims to Him.
JISHUMI:v4p2453#2/r23.anchor: أي: في هذا التحريم، وأن الكفار كذبوا في ذلك على ربهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r1.claim: A clawed animal is any beast or bird with a toe or digit; some such animals had been lawful before their prohibition as punishment for wrongdoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r1.anchor: ذو الظفر ما له أصبع من دابة أو طائر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r2.claim: The prohibition is explained as punishment for Israel’s wrongdoing, as also stated in 4:160.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r2.anchor: بدليل قوله : { فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r3.claim: They were forbidden the meat and fat of every clawed animal, but cattle and sheep remained lawful except for their pure fats, including large and kidney fats.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r3.anchor: والمعنى أنه حرم عليهم لحم كل ذي ظفر وشحمه كل شيء منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r4.claim: The permitted exception is the thin fat covering the backs and flanks.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r4.anchor: يعني إلا ما اشتمل على الظهور والجنوب من السحفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r5.anchor: أو الحوايا } أو اشتمل على الأمعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r6.claim: The fat mixed with bone is the fat of the tail.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r6.anchor: أو ما اختلط بعظم } وهو شحم الإلية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r7.claim: The partitive ‘min’ supplies an added connection, as in ‘I took his property from Zayd,’ strengthening the relation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r7.anchor: كقولك : من زيد أخذت ماله ، تريد الإضافة زيادة الربط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r8.claim: One parsing coordinates ‘al-ḥawāyā’ with ‘their fats’; ‘or’ can work as in ‘sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r8.anchor: وقيل : { الحوايا } عطف على شحومهما . و ( أو ) بمنزلتها في قولهم : جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r9.claim: ‘That’ refers to the punishment, namely the prohibition of good things.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r9.anchor: { ذالك } الجزاء { جزيناهم } وهو تحريم الطيبات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r10.claim: Their transgression is the reason for the prohibition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r10.anchor: وهو تحريم الطيبات { ببغيهم } بسبب ظلمهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r11.claim: God does not break threats against sinners any more than promises to the obedient; their disobedience brought the threatened punishment upon them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p71/r11.anchor: { وإنا لصادقون } فيما أوعدنا به العصاة لا نخلفه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r1.claim: The prohibition imposed on the Jews is a trial and a punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r1.anchor: هذا التحريم على الذين هادوا إنما هو تكليف بلوى وعقوبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، مجاهد، قتادة، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r2.claim: One view defines every possessor of a nail as animals whose toes are not split, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r2.anchor: ما ليس منفرج الأصابع كالإبل والنعام والأوز والبط , قاله ابن عباس , وسعيد بن جبير , ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r3.claim: A second view interprets the phrase as all kinds of predatory beasts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r3.anchor: والثاني : أنه عنى أنواع السباع كلها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r4.claim: A third view includes every bird with a claw and every beast with a hoof.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r4.anchor: والثالث : أنه كل ذي مخلب من الطير , وكل ذي حافر من الدواب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r5.claim: Qatada limits the forbidden fat to the fat of the omentum or rump.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r5.anchor: أنها شحوم الثرب خاصة , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the forbidden fat is any fat neither mixed with bone nor on a bone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r6.anchor: أنه كل شحم لم يكن مختلطا بعظم ولا على عظم , قاله ابن جريج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r7.speaker: السدي، ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r7.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd identify the forbidden fat as that of the omentum and kidneys.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r7.anchor: أنه شحم الثرب والكلى , قاله السدي وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r8.claim: The exception includes flank fat and fat attached to the back, which was not forbidden to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r8.anchor: يعني شحم الجنب وما علق بالظهر فإنه لم يحرم عليهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، سعيد بن جبير، قتادة، مجاهد، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r9.claim: One view identifies al-hawaya as the bowels or viscera.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r9.anchor: أنها المباعر , قاله ابن عباس , والحسن , وسعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r10.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r10.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says al-hawaya means the udder glands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r10.anchor: والثاني : أنها بنات اللبن , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r11.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r11.claim: Another view says al-hawaya are intestines with fat on their inner side.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r11.anchor: أنها الأمعاء التي عليها الشحم من داخلها , قاله بعض المتأخرين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r12.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r12.claim: Ali ibn Isa takes al-hawaya as everything that gathers and curves within the belly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r12.anchor: أنها كل ما تحوى في البطن واجتمع واستدار , قاله علي بن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r13.claim: One view of what was permitted is flank fat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r14.speaker: ابن جريج، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r14.claim: Another view includes flank and buttock fat because the latter lies on the coccyx.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r14.anchor: أنه شحم الجنب والألية , لأنه على العصعص , قاله ابن جريج , والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r15.claim: One explanation says the punishment was for their wrong against Moses in their demands and disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r15.anchor: ببغيهم على موسى عليه السلام فيما اقترحوه وعلى ما خالفوه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r16.claim: A second explanation says they wronged themselves by forbidding what had been lawful to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r16.anchor: ببغيهم على أنفسهم في الحلال الذي حرموه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p183/r17.claim: God is truthful in what He reports about them and in what He prohibited for them.

MUQATIL:6:145-147/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r8.claim: The Jews' “every clawed animal” includes camels, ostriches, geese, ducks, and other animals or birds with hooves or claws.
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r8.anchor: { وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر } ، يعني الإبل، والنعامة، والوز، والبط، وكل شىء له خف وظفر من الدواب والطير،

MUQATIL:6:145-147/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r9.claim: The fats of cattle and sheep were forbidden to the Jews, except for the specified parts.
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r9.anchor: { ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما } ، وحرم عليهم الشحوم من البقر والغنم،

MUQATIL:6:145-147/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r10.claim: Fat on the backs and shoulders and the sheep's rump was permitted to them.
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r10.anchor: { إلا ما حملت ظهورهما } ، يعني ظهور البقر والغنم والأكتاف والإلية،

MUQATIL:6:145-147/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r12.claim: Fat mixed with bone was permitted, whereas kidney fat and the fat called thurūb were prohibited.
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r12.anchor: { أو ما اختلط } من الشحم { بعظم } ، فكل هذا حلال لهم، وحرم عليهم شحوم الكليتين والثروب،

MUQATIL:6:145-147/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r13.claim: This prohibition punished their transgression: killing prophets, blocking God's way, taking usury, and unlawfully taking people's property.
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r13.anchor: { ذلك } التحريم، { جزيناهم ببغيهم } ، يعني عقوبة بقتلهم الأنبياء وبصدهم عن سبيل الله، وبأكلهم الربا،

MUQATIL:6:145-147/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r14.claim: God truthfully revealed to Muḥammad what was forbidden, some prohibitions for Muslims and some for Jews.
MUQATIL:6:145-147/r14.anchor: { وإنا لصادقون } [آية: 146] بذلك، وهذا ما أوحى الله إلى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه محرم، منه على المسلمين، ومنه على اليهود.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r1.claim: Every clawed animal or bird is included, among them camels and ostriches.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r1.anchor: أى ماله أصبع من دابة أو طائر ويدخل فيه الإبل والنعام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r2.claim: The Jews were forbidden the meat and fat of every clawed animal; from cattle and sheep, only their fat was forbidden.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r2.anchor: حرمنا عليهم لحم كل ذى ظفر وشحمه وكل شيء منه ولم يحرم من البقر والغنم إلا الشحوم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r3.claim: The exception includes fat around the back and sides, the entrails, and fat mixed with bone, such as the tail or marrow.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ إلا ما حملت ظهورهما ﴾ إلا ما اشتمل على الظهور والجنوب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r4.claim: Ḥawāyā means what encloses the intestines; its singular is ḥāwiyāʾ or ḥawiyya.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ أو الحوايا ﴾ أو ما اشتمل على الامعاء واحدها حاوياء أو حوية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r5.claim: Dhālika is the second object of jazaynāhum: We repaid them with that.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ مفعول ثان لقوله ﴿ جزيناهم ﴾ والتقدير جزيناهم ذلك ﴿ ببغيهم ﴾ بسبب ظلمهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r6.claim: Their prohibition was imposed because of their wrongdoing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r6.anchor: بسبب ظلمهم ﴿ وإنا لصادقون ﴾ فيما أخبرنا به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r7.claim: The author affirms the truth of God's report and cites the pardon and renewed permission for intimacy in 2:187.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p350#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ وإنا لصادقون ﴾ فيما أخبرنا به وكيف نشكر من سبب معصيتهم لتحريم الحلال ومعصية سالفنا لتحليل الحرام حيث قال وعفا عنكم فالآن باشروهن

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r1.claim: The restrictions on Jews follow the dietary rules for Muhammad's community and refute Jewish claims that God had prohibited nothing, since Israel supposedly imposed the rules himself; these restrictions were a trial and punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r1.anchor: لما ذكر الله عز وجل ما حرم على أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عقب ذلك بذكر ما حرم على اليهود لما في ذلك من تكذيبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r2.claim: Al-Hasan reads ẓufur with a quiescent fāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r3.speaker: أبو السمال
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r3.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads the word with kasra on ẓāʾ and a quiescent fāʾ; Abu Hatim rejects this reading, though al-Qurtubi says it is a dialect.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال «ظفر» بكسر الظاء وإسكان الفاء. وأنكر أبو حاتم كسر الظاء وإسكان الفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r4.speaker: الجوهري والنحاس والفراء وابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r4.claim: The word has plurals أظفار, أظفور, أظافير, and forms cited by al-Farra; Ibn al-Sikkit uses أظفر for a man with especially long nails, as أشعر describes long hair.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r4.anchor: والجمع أظفار وأظفور وأظافير قاله الجوهري. وزاد النحاس عن الفراء أظافير وأظافرة قال ابن السكيت

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r5.claim: Mujahid and Qatada understand the phrase as animals or birds with undivided toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: «ذي ظفر» ما ليس بمنفرج الأصابع من البهائم والطير مثل الإبل والنعام والإوز والبط.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd limits the phrase to camels.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies camels and ostriches, since an ostrich has a nail like a camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «ذي ظفر» البعير والنعامة لأن النعامة ذات ظفر كالإبل.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r8.claim: Another view includes every bird with talons and every beast with hooves, using ẓufr for a hoof figuratively.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r8.anchor: وقيل: يعني كل ذي مخلب من الطير وذي حافر من الدواب. ويسمى الحافر ظفرا استعارة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r9.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r9.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim says hooves and talons are literally nails in their respective sizes, not metaphors: both are soft bone grown from nourishment and can be cut; the names reflect digging, catching, or grasping.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r9.anchor: وقال الترمذي الحكيم: الحافر ظفر، والمخلب ظفر إلا أن هذا على قدره، وذاك على قدره وليس ههنا استعارة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r10.speaker: قتادة والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r10.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi say the prohibited fats are the fat around the stomach and the kidney fat.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r10.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني الثروب وشحم الكليتين وقاله السدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says all fat not mixed with bone or situated on bone was forbidden; flank fat and tail fat were allowed because the latter lies on the tailbone.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r11.anchor: قال ابن جريج: حرم عليهم كل شحم غير مختلط بعظم أو على عظم، وأحل لهم شحم الجنب والألية لأنه على العصعص.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r12.claim: In the exception, ma is accusative and ẓuhuru is nominative as the subject of ḥamalat.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r12.anchor: «ما» في موضع نصب على الاستثناء «ظهورهما» رفع ب«حملت».

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r13.claim: Al-Hawaya is nominative, coordinated with the backs, meaning what the viscera carry; the definite article replaces an annexation, making the viscera part of what is permitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r13.anchor: في موضع رفع عطف على الظهور أي أو حملت حواياهما، والألف واللام بدل من الإضافة. وعلى هذا تكون الحوايا من جملة ما أحل.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r14.speaker: الكسائي والفراء وأحمد بن يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r14.claim: Al-Kisai, al-Farra, and Ahmad ibn Yahya coordinate the phrase with ما حملت; al-Qurtubi calls this the soundest parsing, since coordination normally joins the nearest item unless sense or evidence dictates otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146/r14.anchor: هذا أصح ما قيل فيه. وهو قول الكسائي والفراء وأحمد بن يحيى. والنظر يوجب أن يعطف الشيء على ما يليه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r1.claim: An alternative takes only the back-carried fat as excepted, coordinating the viscera and fat mixed with bone with the prohibited fats.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: إن الإستثناء في التحليل إنما هو ما حملت الظهور خاصة، وقوله: «أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم» معطوف على المحرم.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r2.claim: Al-Shafii uses the exception for back fat to argue that someone who swears not to eat fat breaks the oath by eating that fat.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r2.anchor: احتج الشافعي بهذه الآية في أن من حلف ألا يأكل الشحم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and others identify al-hawaya as the intestines, a plural of mabʿar because dung gathers there; reported singulars include hawiyaʾ, hawiyah, and huwiyyah.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس وغيره. وهو جمع مبعر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda explains hawaya as what folds around the belly, that is, what is rounded.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الحوايا ما تحوى من البطن أي استدار. وهي منحوية أي مستديرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r5.claim: Another explanation takes hawaya as the milk reservoirs connected to the intestines.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: الحوايا خزائن اللبن، وهو يتصل بالمباعر وهي المصارين.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r6.claim: Another explanation identifies hawaya as intestines on which fat lies.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: الحوايا الأمعاء التي عليها الشحوم.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r7.claim: Elsewhere hawaya can mean a cloth wrapped around a camel's hump; Imru al-Qays uses the word in a verse about such camel gear.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r7.anchor: والحوايا في غير هذا الموضع: كساء يحوى حول سنام البعير. قال امرؤ القيس: جعلن حوايا واقتعدن قعائدا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r8.claim: The Torah listed carrion, blood, pork, animals without split hooves, and fish without scales as forbidden; Muhammad's law abrogated these restrictions, lifted hardship, and established Islam's commands and prohibitions.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r8.anchor: فأخبر الله سبحانه أنه كتب عليهم تحريم هذا في التوراة ردا لكذبهم. ونصه فيها: «حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r9.claim: The former prohibitions on animals were abrogated by Muhammad's law, which restored permission and removed hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r9.anchor: ثم نسخ الله ذلك كله بشريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. وأباح لهم ما كان محرما عليهم من الحيوان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r10.speaker: مالك في كتاب محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r10.claim: Malik says fat prohibited to Jews in their own Torah remains prohibited to Muslims when they slaughter it, since they hold it forbidden and do not intend it at slaughter, like blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r10.anchor: قال مالك في كتاب محمد: هي محرمة. وقال في سماع المبسوط: هي محللة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r11.speaker: مالك في سماع المبسوط وابن نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r11.claim: In al-Mabsut, Malik says the fats are permitted, as does Ibn Nafi; Ibn al-Qasim disapproves. The permissive argument is that Islam lifted the restriction and their mistaken belief has no legal effect.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r11.anchor: وقال في سماع المبسوط: هي محللة وبه قال ابن نافع. وقال ابن القاسم: أكرهه.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r12.claim: At Khaybar, Ibn Mughaffal seized a skin of fat and clung to it; the Prophet saw him and smiled. Al-Qurtubi cites the Bukhari and Muslim versions as evidence that the Prophet neither ordered him to discard it nor forbade eating it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r12.anchor: ما رواه الصحيحان عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: كنا محاصرين قصر خيبر، فرمى إنسان بجراب فيه شحم فنزوت لآخذه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r13.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r13.claim: Scholars explain that the Prophet smiled at Ibn Mughaffal's eagerness and reluctance to share the fat.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r13.anchor: قال علماؤنا: تبسمه عليه السلام إنما كان لما رأى من شدة حرص ابن مغفل على أخذ الجراب ومن ضنته به

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي وعامة العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa, al-Shafii, and most scholars permit eating such fat; Malik dislikes it because scholars disagree.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#2/r14.anchor: وعلى جواز الأكل مذهب أبي حنيفة والشافعي وعامة العلماء غير أن مالكا كرهه للخلاف فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r1.speaker: ابن المنذر عن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits Malik's prohibition, followed by senior Maliki authorities on the stated rationale; al-Qurtubi says the Khaybar hadith refutes them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r1.anchor: وحكى ابن المنذر عن مالك تحريمها وإليه ذهب كبراء أصحاب مالك. ومتمسكهم ما تقدم، والحديث حجة عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r2.speaker: أصبغ وأشهب وابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r2.claim: Asbagh, Ashhab, and Ibn al-Qasim say meat of animals that God's Book forbids Jews to eat is not lawful from their slaughter because they hold it forbidden; Ibn Wahb permits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r2.anchor: قال أصبغ: ما كان محرما في كتاب الله من ذبائحهم فلا يحل أكله لأنهم يدينون بتحريمها. وقاله أشهب وابن القاسم، وأجازه ابن وهب.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r3.speaker: ابن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r3.claim: Ibn Habib distinguishes what Muslims know from scripture to be forbidden, which is unlawful from Jewish slaughter, from rules known only through Jewish reports or reasoning, which are not forbidden to Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب: ما كان محرما عليهم، وعلمنا ذلك من كتابنا فلا يحل لنا من ذبائحهم، وما لم نعلم تحريمه إلا من أقوالهم واجتهادهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r4.claim: Dhalika refers to the prohibition and is nominative, as the predicate in the implied statement: the matter is that.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r4.anchor: أي ذلك التحريم. فذلك في موضع رفع، أي الأمر ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r5.claim: Their restrictions were punishment for wrongdoing, including killing prophets, obstructing God's path, taking usury, and appropriating people's wealth unlawfully.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r5.anchor: عقوبة لهم لقتلهم الأنبياء وصدهم عن سبيل الله، وأخذهم الربا واستحلالهم أموال الناس بالباطل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r6.claim: The verse shows that prohibition comes as a consequence of sin: since it narrows what is allowed, such restriction follows accountability.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r6.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن التحريم إنما يكون بذنب لأنه ضيق فلا يعدل عن السعة إليه إلا عند المؤاخذة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r7.claim: God is truthful in reporting which meats and fats He prohibited to those Jews.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:146#3/r7.anchor: { وإنا لصادقون } في إخبارنا عن هؤلا اليهود عما حرمنا عليهم من اللحوم والشحوم.

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r1.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies every ذو ظفر as camels alone.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس : أنه الإبل فقط .

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r2.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies camels and ostriches; Mujāhid holds the same view.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r2.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس : أنه الإبل والنعامة ، وهو قول مجاهد .

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r3.claim: Ibn Muslim includes every clawed bird and hoofed animal in the phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسلم : إنه كل ذي مخلب من الطير وكل ذي حافر من الدواب .

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the hoof reading because hoof is not ordinarily called a nail and would wrongly include cattle and sheep.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r4.anchor: وأقول : أماحمل الظفر على الحافر فبعيد من وجهين : الأول : أن الحافر لا يكاد يسمى ظفرا .

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī takes the term as claws and talons, encompassing predators, dogs, cats, and hunting birds.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r5.anchor: وجب حمل الظفر على المخالب والبراثن لأن المخالب آلات الجوارح في الاصطياد والبراثن آلات السباع في الاصطياد

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r6.claim: The wording restricts this ban to Jews: it conveys exclusivity, and a universal ban would make the specification pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r6.anchor: يفيد تخصيص هذه الحرمة بهم من وجهين : الأول : أن قوله : { وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا } كذا وكذا يفيد الحصر في اللغة .

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the report that the Prophet forbade every fanged predator and clawed bird: it is a solitary report contrary to the Book.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r7.anchor: ما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم حرم كل ذي ناب من السباع وذي مخلب من الطيور ضعيف لأنه خبر واحد على خلاف كتاب الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r8.claim: This reading of the verse strengthens Mālik's position that these animals are not forbidden to Muslims.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا التقدير : يقوى قول مالك في هذه المسألة .

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r9.claim: The verse next describes cattle and sheep fat as a separate category forbidden specifically to Jews, with three exceptions.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r9.anchor: النوع الثاني : من الأشياء التي حرمها الله تعالى على اليهود خاصة ، قوله تعالى : { ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما }

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says fat attached to the back is exempt from the prohibition.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس : إلا ما علق بالظهر من الشحم ، فإني لم أحرمه

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r11.claim: Qatāda includes fat attached to the back and flank from within the abdomen.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة : إلا ما علق بالظهر والجنب / من داخل بطونها

RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r12.claim: Al-Rāzī identifies the permitted attached layer as white fatty meat adjoining red meat; eating it breaks an oath not to eat fat.
RAZI-FULL:v13p182#2/r12.anchor: ليس على الظهر والجنب شحم إلا اللحم الأبيض السمين الملتصق باللحم الأحمر

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī glosses al-ḥawāyā as abomasums and intestines, with singular forms ḥāwiya and ḥawiyya.
