RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : وهي المباعر والمصارين ، واحدتها حاوية وحوية .

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r2.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says it is the ḥawiyya or ḥāwiya, the coiled part inside a sheep's belly.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي : هي الحوية أو الحاوية ، وهي الدوارة التي في بطن الشاة .

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt gives ḥāwiya and ḥawāyā, patterned like riwāya and rawāyā.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r3.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت : يقال حاوية وحوايا ، مثل رواية وروايا .

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r4.claim: On the first syntactic reading, fats adhering to the viscera and intestines are not forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r4.anchor: فالمراد أن الشحوم الملتصقة بالمباعر والمصارين غير محرمة .

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r5.speaker: جميع المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r5.claim: All commentators identify what is mixed with bone as tail fat.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r5.anchor: قالوا : إنه شحم الإلية في قول جميع المفسرين .

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj includes fat in the leg, flank, head, eyes, and ears; on this account, prohibited fat is the omentum and kidney fat.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : كل شحم في القائم والجنب والرأس ، وفي العينين والأذنيين .

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r7.claim: An alternative parsing coordinates al-ḥawāyā and what is mixed with bone with the prohibited fats, leaving only back fat exempt.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r7.anchor: غير معطوف على المستثنى ، بل على المستثنى منه والتقدير : حرمت عليهم شحومهما

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r8.claim: This parsing uses aw as in the command not to obey a sinner or disbeliever, where either can be disobeyed.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r8.anchor: ودخلت كلمة ( أو ) كدخولها في قوله تعالى : { ولا تطع منهم ءاثما أو كفورا } ( الإنسان : 24 )

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r9.claim: The special prohibition repays their oppression, including killing prophets, taking usury, and consuming property unjustly.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r9.anchor: والمعنى : أنا إنما خصصناهم بهذا التحريم جزاء على بغيهم ، وهو قتلهم الأنبياء ، وأخذهم الربا

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r10.claim: The same rationale appears where God says good things were forbidden to the Jews for their wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r10.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم } ( النساء : 160 )

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r11.claim: God is truthful both about their oppression and about making the prohibition specific to them because of it.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r11.anchor: أي في الأخبار عن بغيهم وفي الأخبار عن تخصيصهم بهذا التحريم بسبب بغيهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r12.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r12.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that prohibition cannot punish a prior offense, since legal obligation offers reward and is a beneficence.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r12.anchor: قال القاضي : نفس التحريم لا يجوز أن يكون عقوبة على جرم صدر عنهم ، لأن التكليف تعريض للثواب

RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that withholding a benefit can increase deserved reward or punish a prior offense; both are plausible.
RAZI-FULL:v13p183/r13.anchor: فالجواب : أن المنع من الانتفاع يمكن أن يكون لمزيد استحقاق الثواب ، ويمكن أيضا أن يكون للجرم المتقدم

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r1.claim: After criticizing Makkan restrictions and listing four revealed prohibitions, the verse adds Jewish dietary bans as recompense for disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r1.anchor: After the criticisms of the arbitrary restrictions on eating meat observed by the Makkan idolaters

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r2.claim: The phrase suggests a ban on all carnivorous beasts, a prohibition also incorporated into Islamic dietary law through Prophetic Sunnah.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r2.anchor: suggests that they are forbidden all carnivorous beasts

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r3.speaker: commentators (JJ, Q, Ṭ)
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r3.claim: Many Quranic commentators understand dhī ẓufur as animals with undivided toes rather than claws.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r3.anchor: to mean “with undivided toes” (JJ, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r4.claim: The Jews were forbidden ox and sheep fat except back fat, fat in the entrails, or fat mingled with other tissue.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r4.anchor: They are further forbidden the fat of oxen and sheep, except for that upon their backs or intermingled with other tissue

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r5.speaker: Abū Ḥanīfah and al-Shāfiʿī
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r5.claim: These two Sunni school founders held that the fat prohibition did not apply to Muslims.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r5.anchor: Abū Ḥanīfah and al-Shāfiʿī, held that this prohibition on fat did not pertain to Muslims

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet did not forbid a follower from eating fat during the siege of Khaybar, when he imposed other food prohibitions.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r6.anchor: the Prophet did not forbid one of his followers from eating it during the siege of Khaybar

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r7.claim: The Jewish restrictions largely parallel, but do not exactly match, dietary prohibitions in Leviticus and Deuteronomy.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r7.anchor: The specific dietary prohibitions mentioned for the Jews in the present verse are largely consistent with the extensive dietary prohibitions found in Leviticus 3 and 11, as well as Deuteronomy 14, although they are not identical

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r8.claim: Leviticus 11 bans animals that walk on paws and several birds of prey, as well as animals with undivided hooves such as camels.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r8.anchor: the Israelites are forbidden “all that walk on their paws” (v. 27) and several different birds of prey, but also animals with undivided hooves, such as camels

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r9.claim: Leviticus instructs the Israelites to remove backbone and entrail fat for burning as sacrifice.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r9.anchor: the Israelites are instructed to remove the fat from the backbone and the entrails to be burned as a sacrifice

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r10.speaker: Ṭb
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r10.claim: One gloss explains their willful disobedience as mistreatment of needy people among themselves.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r10.anchor: their mistreatment of the needy among themselves (Ṭb)

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r11.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r11.claim: Another gloss takes their willful disobedience simply as wrongdoing.

STUDYQURAN:6:146/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r12.claim: Quran 3:93 says no divinely imposed food prohibitions applied to Israelites before the Torah was revealed.
STUDYQURAN:6:146/r12.anchor: indicates that there were no Divinely imposed dietary prohibitions on the Israelites prior to the revelation of the Torah

TABATABAI:6:142-146/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r11.claim: Every clawed animal means one having a nail-like bone growing at the tips of its fingers.
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r11.anchor: الظفر واحد الأظفار وهو العظم النابت على رؤوس الأصابع

TABATABAI:6:142-146/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r12.claim: Al-hawaya means the entrails, or bowels.

TABATABAI:6:142-146/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r13.claim: Al-Majma' offers nominative coordination of al-hawaya with ‘backs’ or accusative coordination with the object of ‘carried’; al-Tabataba'i prefers the nominative. The phrase ‘what mixed with bone’ coordinates with the first ‘what.’
TABATABAI:6:142-146/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون نصبا عطفا على ما في قوله

TABATABAI:6:146-149/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:146-149/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:146-149/r1.claim: In ذلك جزيناهم, ذلك may be the second object of جزيناهم; making it a subject requires an unexpressed pronoun and is acceptable only by poetic necessity.
TABATABAI:6:146-149/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون منصوب الموضع بأنه مفعول ثان لجزيناهم التقدير جزيناهم ذلك ببغيهم، ولا يجوز أن يرفع بالإبتداء

TABATABAI:6:146-149/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:146-149/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:146-149/r2.claim: The restrictions on Israel were punishment for rebellion, so they do not contradict these foods having been originally permissible by nature.
TABATABAI:6:146-149/r2.anchor: ما حرم الله على بني إسرائيل من طيبات ما رزقهم إنما حرمه جزاء لبغيهم فلا ينافي

TABATABAI:6:136-150#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:136-150#3/r4.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
TABATABAI:6:136-150#3/r4.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports that Israelite rulers barred poor people from bird meat and fats, so God prohibited these foods because of the rulers' oppression of the poor; the report is attributed to ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm's tafsīr.
TABATABAI:6:136-150#3/r4.anchor: إن ملوك بني إسرائيل كانوا يمنعون فقراءهم من أكل لحوم الطير والشحوم فحرم الله ذلك ببغيهم على فقرائهم. ذكره علي بن إبراهيم في تفسيره

AKHFASH:v1p316/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p316/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p316/r2.claim: الحوايا has the singular forms الحاوياء and الحاوية.

AKHFASH:v1p316/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p316/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p316/r3.claim: The construction means 'and We prohibited cattle and sheep to them'; من is inserted as Arabs sometimes say كان من حديث for كان حديث.
AKHFASH:v1p316/r3.anchor: ولكنه أدخل فيها "من" والعرب تقول: "قد كان من حديث"

AKHFASH:v1p316/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p316/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p316/r4.claim: Alternatively, من may be partitive: from the sheep We prohibited the fats, like taking a half from a house or striking a man's face.
AKHFASH:v1p316/r4.anchor: وإن شئت قلت: "ومن الغنم حرمنا الشحوم" كما تقول: "من الدار أخذ النصف والثلث"

TABRISI:6:146-147/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147/r1.claim: Ẓufr means a nail or claw; a person with long nails is called aẓfar, by analogy with aʿshar for someone with long hair.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r1.anchor: الظفر ظفر الإنسان وغيره ورجل أظفر إذا كان طويل الأظفار

TABRISI:6:146-147/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:146-147/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives the singulars of ḥawāyā as ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, and ḥawiyya, for what gathers and coils inside the belly.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r2.anchor: واحدها حاوية وحاوياء وحوية وهي ما يحوى في البطن

TABRISI:6:146-147/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147/r3.claim: Al-ḥawāyā can be nominative, coordinated with ẓuhūrihimā, or accusative, coordinated with the object after illā; mā ikhtalaṭa is likewise coordinated with that object.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r3.anchor: موضع الحوايا يحتمل أن يكون رفعا عطفا على الظهور

TABRISI:6:146-147/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147/r4.claim: Dhālika is best parsed in the accusative as the second object of jazaynāhum; parsing it as a subject would produce a construction only allowed in poetic necessity.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r4.anchor: مفعول ثان لجزيناهم التقدير جزيناهم ذلك ببغيهم

TABRISI:6:146-147/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147/r5.claim: The restrictions described were imposed on the Jews in Moses' time.

TABRISI:6:146-147/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī include animals without split toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r6.anchor: كل ما ليس بمنفرج الأصابع كالإبل والنعام والأوز والبط عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

TABRISI:6:146-147/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:6:146-147/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the phrase to camels.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r7.anchor: هو الإبل فقط عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:6:146-147/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r8.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r8.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī includes predators, dogs, cats, and animals that hunt with claws.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r8.anchor: يدخل فيه كل السباع والكلاب والسنانير وما يصطاد بظفره عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:146-147/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r9.speaker: القُتيبي والبلخي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r9.claim: Al-Qutaybī and al-Balkhī include every clawed bird and every hoofed animal.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r9.anchor: كل ذي مخلب من الطير وكل ذي حافر من الدواب عن القتيبي والبلخي

TABRISI:6:146-147/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147/r10.claim: God forbade Jews the fat of cattle and sheep, including the caul, kidney fat, and other fat inside them.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r10.anchor: أنه كان حرم عليهم شحوم البقر والغنم من الثرب وشحم الكلى

TABRISI:6:146-147/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147/r11.claim: Fat borne on the backs was excepted; the text describes it as the fatty flesh, which was not forbidden.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r11.anchor: من الشحم وهو اللحم السمين فإنه لم يحرم عليهم

TABRISI:6:146-147/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī identify al-ḥawāyā as the intestines or abdominal organs; their fat was likewise excepted.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r12.anchor: والحوايا هي المباعر عن ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

TABRISI:6:146-147/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:6:146-147/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets al-ḥawāyā as the milk-producing glands.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r13.anchor: وقيل: هي بنات اللبن عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:6:146-147/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r14.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r14.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes al-ḥawāyā as the intestines on which fat lies.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r14.anchor: وقيل: هي الأمعاء التي عليها الشحوم عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:146-147/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r15.speaker: ابن جريج والسدي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r15.claim: Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddī say the exception includes the flank fat and the rump fat attached to the coccyx.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r15.anchor: وهو شحم الجنب والألية لأنه على العصعص عن ابن جريج والسدي

TABRISI:6:146-147/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147/r16.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:146-147/r16.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the rump was not included, because it was not named in the exception and the coccyx does not count as bone here.
TABRISI:6:146-147/r16.anchor: الألية لم تدخل في هذا لأنها لم تستثن عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r2.claim: The prohibitions punished Israel for killing prophets, taking usury, and wrongfully consuming people’s property, paralleling 4:160.
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r2.anchor: حرمنا ذلك عليهم عقوبة لهم بقتلهم الأنبياء وأخذهم الربا واستحلالهم أموال الناس بالباطل

TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r3.claim: An alternative gloss takes their wrongdoing as prohibited acts by which they wronged themselves.
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: بغيهم ظلمهم على أنفسهم في ارتكابهم المحظورات

TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r4.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm says Israelite rulers deprived the poor of fowl and fat, so God prohibited those foods because of their oppression.
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r4.anchor: كانوا يمنعون فقراءهم من أكل لحوم الطير والشحوم فحرم الله ذلك ببغيهم على فقرائهم ذكره علي بن إبراهيم

TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r5.claim: Though obligations serve a benefit and expose people to reward, this prohibition is called punishment because their grave sin required changing the benefit; lesser guilt would not have required it.
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r5.anchor: ويسأل فيقال كيف يكون التكليف عقوبة وهو تابع للمصلحة وتعريض للثواب وجوابه إنه إنما سمي جزاء وعقابا

TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r6.claim: God is truthful about the prohibition, their wrongdoing, and everything; it punished earlier generations and benefited later ones until abrogation.
TABRISI:6:146-147#2/r6.anchor: أي في الإخبار عن التحريم وعن بغيهم وفي كل شيء وفي أن ذلك التحريم عقوبة لأوائلهم ومصلحة لمن بعدهم إلى وقت النسخ

FARRA:v1p363/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p363/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p363/r4.claim: The forbidden fats of cattle and sheep include the caul and kidney fat.

FARRA:v1p363/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p363/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p363/r5.claim: ما in the exception “except what their backs carry” is accusative as the object of the verb in the exception.
FARRA:v1p363/r5.anchor: ثم قال: إلا ما حملت ظهورهما و (ما) في موضع نصب بالفعل

FARRA:v1p363/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p363/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p363/r6.claim: الحوايا are the entrails and milk sacs.
FARRA:v1p363/r6.anchor: و (الحوايا) في موضع رفع، تردها على الظهور: إلا ما حملت ظهورهما

FARRA:v1p363/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p363/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p363/r7.claim: الحوايا may be nominative, coordinated with the backs; it may instead be accusative with omitted شحوم, as in “ask the town” for its inhabitants.
FARRA:v1p363/r7.anchor: والنصب على أن تريد (أو شحوم الحوايا) فتحذف الشحوم وتكتفى

FARRA:v1p363/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p363/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p363/r8.claim: What is mixed with bone refers to tail fat, and ما is accusative.
FARRA:v1p363/r8.anchor: وقوله: أو ما اختلط بعظم وهى الألية. و (ما) فى موضع نصب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi lists forms ظفر with fāʾ vowelled or quiescent, reports Hasan's kasra on ẓāʾ with quiescent fāʾ, and Abu al-Sammal's kasra on both; أظفور is another form, attested in poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r1.anchor: في الظفر لغات: ظفر بضم الفاء وهو أعلاها، وظفر بسكون الفاء، وظفر بكسر الظاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the forbidden animals as camels and ostriches; al-Zajjaj prefers this explanation, and Ibn Abbas says ostriches have nails like camels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: (هو البعير والنعامة) (¬2)، وهو قول مجاهد (¬3)، واختيار الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r3.claim: Qatada defines the prohibition broadly as every creature whose toes are not split.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: (كل ذي ظفر ليس بمشقوق الأصابع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj lists camel, ostrich, duck, goose, and wild ass as unsplit-footed and forbidden, contrasting them with split-footed fowl such as chicken and sparrows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r4.anchor: كل ذي ظفر لم يفرج قوائمه من البهائم كالبعير والنعامة والبط والأوز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r5.claim: Abd Allah ibn Muslim says the phrase means birds with talons and beasts with hooves; calling the hoof a nail is metaphorical, as poetry calls it a foot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r5.anchor: أي: كل ذي مخلب من الطير، وكل ذي حافر من الدواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r6.claim: Abd Allah ibn Muslim cites poetry describing a hoof as a foot to support the figurative use of nail for hoof.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r7.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r7.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd restricts the forbidden animal to camels alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p501/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: (يريد: الإبل) (¬3)، وهو قول ابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r1.claim: The commentators identify the forbidden fats as the omenta and kidney fats; Ibn Abbas calls them the internal fats.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says fat attached to the animals' backs was excluded from the prohibition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (إلا ما علق بالظهر من الشحم فإني لم أحرمه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r3.claim: Qatada includes fat attached to the back and side from within the animals' bellies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: (ما علق بالظهر والجنب من داخل بطونهما)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r4.claim: Al-Hawāyā means the bowels and intestines; its singular forms include hāwiya, ḥawiya, and ḥawiyāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r4.anchor: الحوايا} وهي المباعر والمصارين، واحدتها حاوية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi defines the word as the circular coil in a sheep's belly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r5.anchor: هي الحوية والحاوية، وهي الدوارة التي في بطن الشاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r6.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit gives hāwiya and ḥawiya as singulars of ḥawāyā, compares the pattern with zawiya/zawāyā and rāwiya/rawāyā, and records hāwiyāʾ as another singular.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r6.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: (يقال: حاوية وحوايا مثل زاوية وزوايا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r7.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit also records ḥawiya for the pack-like saddle placed on a camel's back for riding.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r7.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: حوية وحوايا مثل الحوية التي توضع على ظهر البعير ويركب فوقها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r8.speaker: جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r8.claim: Jarir's verse uses ḥāwiyāʾ in describing the place where small reptiles feed, as poetic evidence for the word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r8.anchor: وأنشد قول جرير: تضغو الخنانيص والغول التي أكلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari cites a verse using ḥawāyāʾ in a comparison with the hissing of snakes and scorpions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r10.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r10.claim: Abu Ali gives three possible singulars and explains that the plural is fawāʿil from hāwiya/hāwiyāʾ or faʿāʾil from ḥawiya; the latter passes through ḥawāʾi before sound change.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: (الحوايا واحدتها حوية وحاوياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r11.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r11.claim: Abu Ali explains that ḥawāʾi becomes ḥawāyā: a final yāʾ preceded by kasra shifts to alif, and the hamza shifts to yāʾ to avoid adjacent similar letters; compare the hamza discussion at 7:10.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p503/r11.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: (الحوايا واحدتها حوية وحاوياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r1.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r1.claim: Qatada says the exception means what the intestines carried; Ibn Abbas's gloss treats the intestines and what is mixed with bone as fat left unprohibited.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi parses al-hawāyā as coordinated with the subject backs in the nominative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r2.anchor: عطف على الظهور في موضع رفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r3.claim: Al-Farra allows an accusative parse by ellipsis: understand fat of the intestines, deleting fat as in the command to ask the town, meaning its inhabitants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بتقدير حذف المضاف على أن تريد أو شحوم الحوايا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r4.claim: Al-Farra confirms that ḍawʿ is coordinated with naʾīm, not al-būm, just as al-hawāyā is coordinated with mā, not the backs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p506/r4.anchor: يذهب إلى أن الضوع عطف على النئيم، ولم يعطف على البوم كما عطفت (الحوايا) على ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r1.claim: All commentators identify what is mixed with bone as the fat of the tail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r1.anchor: يعني: شحم الألية، في قول جميع المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj includes fat in the limbs, flank, head, eyes, and ears, which people deemed permissible as mixed with bone; only omentum and kidney fat were prohibited.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج: (كل شحم في القوائم والجنب والرأس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r3.claim: Al-Farra parses mā as an accusative coordinated with the earlier exception, what the backs carried; this is the majority exegetical analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: (و (ما) في موضع نصب نسقا على ما في الأولى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq reports an alternative parse: intestines and fat mixed with bone coordinate with the prohibited fats, while only what the backs carried is excepted and permitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (قال قوم: حرمت عليهم الثروب، وأحل لهم ما حملت الظهور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says aw here broadly marks items each worthy of the prohibition or permission in question; unlike wa, it makes clear that any one or all listed items fit the instruction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p508/r5.anchor: وأو بليغة في هذا المعنى؛ لأنك إذا قلت: لا تطع زيدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi explains that this prohibition was their recompense for transgression.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r2.claim: Mujahid specifies their transgression as killing prophets, taking usury, and wrongfully appropriating people's property.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi calls it punishment for their sins and links it to 4:160, where good things were forbidden to the Jews for their wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ({جزيناهم ببغيهم} عاقبناهم بذنوبهم، نظيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r4.claim: God is truthful in reporting both the prohibition and the Jews' transgression.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p510/r4.anchor: أي: في الإخبار عن التحريم وعن بغيهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r1.claim: The prohibited animals include every bird with talons and every animal with an unsplit hoof.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r1.anchor: حرمنا كل ذي ظفر} أي كل ذي مخلب من الطير وكل ذي ظلف ليس بمشقوق.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r2.claim: The fat carried on the animals' backs refers to the fat tail, al-aliyya.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r2.anchor: شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما} يقال: الألية.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r3.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the entrails; their singular forms are ḥāwiya and ḥuwiya.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163/r3.anchor: أو الحوايا} المباعر؛ واحدها حاوية وحوية (1) .

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r4.claim: The animals with a nail or claw prohibited to Jews are camels and ostriches.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r4.anchor: { وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر } يعني: الإبل، والنعامة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r5.claim: Jews were forbidden cattle and sheep fat except fat on the back, in the entrails, or attached to bone.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r5.anchor: { ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا } وهي المباعر { أو ما اختلط بعظم } فإني لم أحرمه.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r6.claim: This prohibition punished their sins, and God truthfully reports the restriction and their wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:144-146/r6.anchor: { ذلك } التحريم { جزيناهم ببغيهم } عاقبناهم بذنوبهم { وإنا لصادقون } في الإخبار عن التحريم، وعن بغيهم

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r1.claim: Zufur means nail, but Arabic distinguishes hoof, split hoof, camel pad, and the claws of predators or predatory birds; whether the word literally covers all is disputed.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r1.anchor: tırnak demektir. Fakat Arapça’da muhtelif hayvanların tırnaklarına ayrı ayrı isimler verilmiş olduğu için

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r2.speaker: Kāmûs
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r2.claim: The lexicon says mihlab is the claw of predatory beasts and hooked claw of predatory birds; one view reserves zufur for non-hunting birds, while the famous view makes it broader than mihlab.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r2.anchor: Kāmûs’ta der ki: “Mıhleb yırtıcı canavarların pençesine ve yırtıcı kuşun çengeline denir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r3.claim: Sparrows and domestic hens unquestionably have zufur; hawks and falcons unquestionably have mihlab, while their inclusion among zufur is disputed.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r3.anchor: serçe, tavuk bi’l-ittifak zî zufur; atmaca, şahin bi’l-ittifak zî mıhleb ve bi’l-ihtilâf zî zufurda dâhildir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r4.claim: Calling hooves zufur is metaphorical but accepted; Turkish tırnak is similarly broad, though the unqualified phrase tırnaklı hayvan colloquially suggests predators.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r4.anchor: hâfire, zılfa zufur veya zî zufur ıtlâkı mecaz olduğu da tefsirlerde beyan olunuyor

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r5.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r5.claim: Rāzī takes the immediately suggested sense as clawed predators, including predatory beasts and birds and hunting animals.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r5.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî bu âyette de bu mânanın mütebâdir olduğuna kāil olmuş

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r6.speaker: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, İbn Cübeyr, Katâde ve Süddî
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r6.claim: These authorities instead identify animals whose toes are not spread out, such as camels, ostriches, ducks, and geese; Zeccâc also prefers this view.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r6.anchor: İbn Abbas ve Mücâhid ve İbn Cübeyr ve Katâde ve Süddî’den ise bunun aksine deve ve deve kuşu ve ördek ve kaz vesâire gibi parmakları açık olmayan hayvanlar diye menkuldür

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r7.speaker: İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase refers specifically to camels.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r7.anchor: İbn Zeyd bundan maksat bilhassa deve olduğunu

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r8.speaker: Dahhâk
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r8.claim: Dahhāk identifies ostriches and wild asses.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r8.anchor: Dahhâk devekuşu ve himâr-ı vahşî olduğunu söylemiştir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r9.speaker: Kelbî
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r9.claim: Kalbī defines the class by animal kind: clawed birds, hoofed quadrupeds, and fanged predators.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r9.anchor: Kelbî “tuyûrdan her zî mıhleb, devâbdan her zî hâfir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r10.speaker: Kutebî
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r10.claim: Kutaybī equates zufur here with hoof and says hoofed quadrupeds are included by metaphor.

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r11.speaker: Sa‘leb
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r11.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes non-hunting animals with zufur from hunting animals with mihlab.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r11.anchor: Sa‘leb “sayd etmeyen zî zufur, sayd eden zî mıhlebdir” demiş

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r12.speaker: Nakkāş
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r12.claim: Naqqāsh objects that Thaʿlab's distinction is not consistent, since lions also have zufur.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r12.anchor: Nakkāş da “bu muttarid değildir, zira arslan zî zufurdur” demiş

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r13.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r13.claim: Zamakhsharī interprets the term as animals with toes, including camels, birds, and predators; many exegetes prefer this view, which excludes one-hoofed horses.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r13.anchor: Zemahşerî de “deve, tuyûr ve sibâ‘gibi parmaklı olanlar” diye tefsir etmiştir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r14.claim: Although most exegetes include camels and hoofs may also be called zufur metaphorically, Elmalılı reads the phrase broadly as all nail-bearing animals except cattle and sheep.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r14.anchor: Bundan dolayı bizim anladığımıza göre كُلَّ ذِى ظُفُرٍۢ bakar ve ganem

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r15.claim: The broad reading fits the contrast: Jews held that animals both cud-chewing and split-hoofed were lawful, leaving other kinds forbidden to them.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r15.anchor: Yahudîler geviş getirmekle beraber çatal tırnağı bulunan hayvanların helâl ve bu iki vasıf bulunmayan hayvânâtın haram olduğunu söylemekte

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r16.claim: That Jewish criterion would also make fish forbidden, although fish were not prohibited to them, showing their own account of the restrictions was inaccurate.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r16.anchor: Hâlbuki balık tahrim edilmemiş olduğu cihetle Yahudîlerin kendi ifadeleri kendilerine haram kılınanların târifi husûsunda sâdık değil demektir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r17.claim: The Qur'an's contrast excludes fish yet signals that the restriction included swine, predators, single-hoofed animals, camels, and all birds, intensifying the Jews' dietary constraint.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#3/r17.anchor: hınzır ve yırtıcı hayvanlarla beraber tek tırnaklıların ve devenin ve bütün kuşların dahi kendilerine haram kılındığını iş‘âr etmektedir

ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r1.claim: The prohibited cattle and sheep fats are suet or caul fat and kidney fat; fats borne on the back, in the entrails, or mixed with bone remain permitted, including tail fat.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r1.anchor: veya havyalarının, yani bağırsaklarının hâmil olduğu yağlar

ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r2.claim: These foods were originally lawful; God later imposed the restriction as punishment for Jewish transgressions, including killing prophets, usury, obstructing the path, consuming illicit wealth, and reversing lawful and unlawful.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r2.anchor: bağy ü zulümleri katl-i enbiyâ, ahz-ı ribâ, hak yolundan men‘, ekl-i suht, helâlı haram

ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r3.claim: God's truthfulness covers reports, promises, and threats, so the report of punitive prohibition is true; those who invert God's rulings ultimately face deprivation.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r3.anchor: İhbârda da sâdıkız, va‘d ü va‘îdde de sâdıkızdır

ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r4.claim: If Jews deny that these restrictions were imposed as punishment, the author points to 3:93 concerning Israel's own earlier restrictions.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r4.anchor: hayır, bize tahrim edilenler böyle değil idi” veya “bu tahrim sonradan bağyimizin cezâsı olarak değil ta aslından böyle idi

ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r7.claim: Divine commands, prohibitions, lawful status, reward, and punishment concern voluntary acts, not acts done under compulsion; decree therefore does not mean sheer determinism.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r7.anchor: emr ü nehiy, hıll ü hurmet, sevâb ü ikāb ıztırâriyyâta değil, ihtiyâriyyâta ta‘alluk eder

ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r8.claim: Ordaining chosen acts means ordaining the servant's choice and ordering divine will with it, not imposing pure compulsion.
ELMALILI:6:143-147#4/r8.anchor: Böyle ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyenin takdir ve halkı ihtiyâr-ı abdi takdir ve meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeyi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r1.claim: For their transgression, Jews alone were forbidden clawed animals and the interior fats of cattle and sheep, with specified exceptions; the preceding verse had given the general meat rule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r1.anchor: Bir önceki âyette hangi hayvanların etlerinin yenileceğine ilişkin genel hüküm belirtildikten sonra burada, azgınlık ve zulümleri sebebiyle sadece yahudilere tırnaklı hayvanların etleriyle sığır ve koyunun iç yağlarının da haram kılındığı belirtilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r2.claim: The author points to Leviticus and Deuteronomy for Jewish dietary permissions and prohibitions on these foods.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:146/r2.anchor: Yahudilik’te bu konuyla ilgili helâller ve haramlar için bk. Levililer, 3/17; 7/23; 11/1 vd.; Tesniye, 14/3 vd.

NAHHAS:v2p104/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r1.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v2p104/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ẓufr with a still fāʾ.

NAHHAS:v2p104/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r2.speaker: أبو السمال
NAHHAS:v2p104/r2.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads ẓufr with still fāʾ and kasra on ẓāʾ; Abū Ḥātim rejects the kasra-plus-sukūn reading.
NAHHAS:v2p104/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال ( ظفر ) بإسكان الفاء وكسر الظاء وأنكر أبو حاتم كسر الظاء

NAHHAS:v2p104/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r3.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p104/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records the plural forms aẓāfīr, aẓāfira, aẓāfir, and aẓfār.
NAHHAS:v2p104/r3.anchor: وحكى الفراء في الجمع أظافير وأظافرة وأظافر وأظفارا

NAHHAS:v2p104/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p104/r4.claim: Mā is accusative as an exception, and ẓuhūruhumā is nominative as the subject of ḥamalat.
NAHHAS:v2p104/r4.anchor: ( ما ) في موضع نصب على الاستثناء ( ظهورهما ) رفع بحملت

NAHHAS:v2p104/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p104/r5.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is nominative coordinated with ẓuhūr; its singular is ḥāwiya, with forms ḥawāyā/ḥawāyāʾ like nāfiqāʾ/nawāfiq and ḍāriba/ḍawārib; a yāʾ becomes alif as in ṣaḥārā.
NAHHAS:v2p104/r5.anchor: حاوية وحوايا وحاوياء مثل نافقاء ونوافق وضاربة وضوارب

NAHHAS:v2p104/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p104/r6.claim: Mā is accusative, coordinated with the nearest mā in mā ḥamalat; al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ, Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, and the syntax support this unless meaning or evidence dictates otherwise.
NAHHAS:v2p104/r6.anchor: وفي هذا أقوال هذا أصحها وهو قول الكسائي والفراء وأحمد بن يحيى والنظر يوجبه أن يعطف الشيء

NAHHAS:v2p104/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p104/r7.claim: Dhālika here means “that is how We repaid them.”

NAHHAS:v2p104/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p104/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p104/r8.claim: The phrase is the predicate of inna; its original form is innanā.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r1.claim: The anemone as ruby flags on emerald spears and stars as pearls on blue carpet are difficult, accomplished similes that reach beyond commonplace comparisons.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r1.anchor: وكأن محمر الشقيق إذا تصوب أو تصعد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r2.claim: A whole impression arrives before its details: first sight gives a general view, and closer attention discloses particulars.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r2.anchor: إحدى العبرتين أنا نعلم أن الجملة أبدا أسبق إلى النفوس من التفصيل وإنك تجد الرؤية نفسها لا تصل بالبديهة إلى التفصيل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r3.claim: Repeated hearing or tasting reveals details missed at first; discerning particulars distinguishes one observer or listener from another.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p136/r3.anchor: فإنك تتبين من تفاصيل الصوت بأن يعاد عليك حتى تسمعه مرة ثانية ما لم تتبينه بالسماع الأول

ITQAN:v2p310/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p310/r24.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p310/r24.claim: What their backs carried refers to fat attached to them.
ITQAN:v2p310/r24.anchor: 1620 ﴿ ما حملت ظهورهما ﴾ ما علق بها من الشحم

NASHR:v1p272/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p272/r3.speaker: فارس بن أحمد وابن مهران
NASHR:v1p272/r3.claim: Faris uniquely reports Yaqub with ḍamma in bi-baghyihim and ḥuliyyihim; Ibn Mihran reports kasra in min aydīhinna wa-arjulihinna, while the other readers use the usual form throughout this section.
NASHR:v1p272/r3.anchor: وانفرد فارس بن أحمد، عن يعقوب بضم الهاء في (ببغيهم) في الأنعام، و (حليهم) في الأعراف

NASHR:v2p265#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p265#2/r8.speaker: فارس بن أحمد
NASHR:v2p265#2/r8.claim: The source recalls Faris ibn Ahmad’s unique reading with damma on the hāʾ of ببغيهم.
NASHR:v2p265#2/r8.anchor: وتقدم انفراد فارس بن أحمد في ضم هاء (ببغيهم)
